text: Tonight, I can write the saddest lines. Write for example, the night is starry, and the blue stars shiver in the distance. The night wind revolves in the sky and sings. Tonight, I can write the saddest lines. I loved her, and sometimes she loved me too. Through nights like this one, I held her in my arms. I kissed her again and again under the endless sky. She loved me sometimes, and I loved her too. How could one not have loved her great still eyes? Tonight, I can write the saddest lines. To think that I do not have her, to feel that I have lost her. To hear the immense night, still more immense without her, and the verse falls to the soul like dew to the pasture. What does it matter that my love could not keep her? The night is starry, and she is not with me. This is all. In the distance, someone is singing. In the distance. My soul is not satisfied that it has lost her. My sight tries to find her as though to bring her closer. My heart looks for her, and she is not with me. The same night whitening the same trees. We of that time are no longer the same. I no longer love her. That's certain, but how I loved her. My voice tried to find the wind to touch her hearing. Another's, she will be another's, as she was before my kisses. Her voice, her bright body, her infinite eyes. I no longer love her, that's certain. But maybe I love her. Love is so short, forgetting is so long. As through the nights like this one, I held her in my arms. My soul is not satisfied that it has lost her. Though this be the last pain that she makes me suffer, and these the last verses that I write for her.

The hardest thing I ever did was take a shower. Holding the body of someone you love who has committed suicide is easy. All you have to do is sit there while you wait for the paramedics and hope that you are wrong, pray that there is still a person here to save. When you are in shock, the weight of a torso is negligible. For all of the strain it puts on your body, you might as well be on the beach holding a book. I think we should redefine the word tragedy as "that which is impossible to get over." Unless you are profoundly lucky, it will happen to you. And on that day, when all of your happy daydreams seem tiny and all of your nightmares seem huge, on the day when the worst what-if you can ever imagine has already happened, when a friend who you love has committed suicide, when your stepfather is paralyzed probably forever-- whatever your tragedy is, please use me as a cautionary tale. Because only a madman tries to do the impossible, and after her death, I was indeed a madman. I tried to get over her suicide, and, failing that, I did nothing. I sat in my own filth for three weeks until a dear friend walked into my room carrying a towel, hoping that I was not another impossible task, and said, "You are taking a shower right now." That shower was the hardest thing I have ever done. You cannot get over somebody, but you can take a shower. And then you can get dressed. And then you can find your keys. And then you can go grocery shopping. And then you can do your laundry. And then it's 10 years later, and they are still dead, and you are happy. I don't believe in God, but I do believe in miracles, in things so large that they seem impossible but when you do them one tiny step at a time, you get them done. Taking a shower is a miracle. Laughing is a miracle. Being here is a miracle. See, that's the real example. We all give up, and we all hide, and we all wallow in our own whatever awful we have to wallow in. But if you're lucky, if there's a miracle, you take a shower, and you get up, and you keep doing tiny things until the world is a slightly less dark place. Thank you.

When you broke my heart, I felt the familiar sting of the pain of loss. The nights became longer and the days were worse. I missed the golden flares of the sunrise in the mornings as I sunk deeper and deeper into the couch, hoping upon hope that you would call me. The phone never rang and there were no texts waiting for me. I had to learn the hard way that no message was also a message. Regret has embraced me like an old friend, rocking me daily now as I get drunk on my salty tears. I spend my days on the edge of rage and it's too risky to be skipping meals and seeking peace in the bottom of this bottle of whiskey. You see, I thought we had had a happy year. There was just so much left that we hadn't shared, but when you said you weren't happy here, it tore me apart to know that I hadn't shown you how much I truly cared. Now all I have are memories from the past year. Collected in JPEGs, just taking up space in folders that I'm afraid to delete because it would signify that we're really done and everything gone. And I guess I'm delusional enough to believe you're still the one. I don't want to get over you. I want to get under you to taste the sweetness of your tongue as you plundered me with your love and ride me like a horse into the sunset. I'm not sorry that I missed a step and tripped and fell hard for you. I'm only sorry that I expected you to love me in a way that I hadn't yet loved myself. But I know now that God had a plan when he sent you to me. It wasn't you who needed my love, it was me. So if the only way I could find a treasure that was buried deep within was to force me open and help me feel, then I guess it was okay that you broke my heart and set me free.

Call this world a manageable canopy. Call my window a faulty drainage passage. Call my skin a raincoat. Training on ways to shield me from this water that stalks the fences of my body. How its cryptic hand calves me a bowl of sweat as a parting gift. There are no dry roads I can find to walk through and back from the world undetected. I wonder if anyone notices my superpower is to flood myself with worry. My room tries to contain me afraid to bother neighbors. I scrounge for any ounce of power in a world I already feel powerless and I shake at the idea of flashlights glowing on my weakness. I remind myself every superhero war disguised only difference is the only person I can't save is myself. My ghost drips inside every photo caption I upload. The walls of my room on audience debates I have with myself on weather to head outside when the sun knocks with its bruised fist. Everything around me feels like it carries water. Everything with water seems to be keeping its eye on me. The radio fuzz is like a robot dropped in an ocean. The wind feels like an invisible tornado. A friend drinks from a glass of water and it spills while attempting to pounce on me. I want to tell her that water has claws but my mouth shuts. I respond to every how you message with I'm good and carry the real answer on my back like a toe in weight. I teeter on thought of tying my tongue to a loud speaker communicating help by any means necessary. All I want is this cloud of water to stop floating above my head. All I want is an umbrella of hand to make me feel the touch of protection.

The poet felt like broken verses, shards of rhymes unmented, Another material girl covered in credit card class, Watered by the storm trickling from the corner of her eye. All the while he was looking his lips, watching his land turning, Like water melting away with a drought, Another farmer withering under the glare of summer. Another unfulfilled promise, leaving him thirsty, Craving, somehow in nations asunder, These two could feel the soul of the other, so familiar. Somehow the symphony of a life-breaking Sounds the same no matter where it begins echoing, The longing to be known and to become knowing, The heart peeling for something better than the common river of sorrow, Running like blood through the veins of our humanity. The empty writer who only wants to fill another paper, The lover of springtime pleasure, forgotten by the winds of winter. The starving farmer, still waiting to see the reward for his labor, The adopted children, wondering about their father, The banker who invested his life and money, But was only left lonely, These created masses who really only want to know their creator, To be known by the Master Potter, A world of broken pieces grasping for the love of a maker. Who knows, maybe life isn't really about us and the enemy, Maybe those calling out left, right, left, right, Are only marching us off to war. Who knows, maybe there is no them, Maybe life really is just about you and me. But what if there were still something greater to consider as a human choir, Whaling songs of hatred and disorder? What if our mutual dissatisfaction with the temporary Is a sign that we were all made for eternity, Something far beyond what we can see, perfect sanity. Wouldn't this, shouldn't this be where we want to be? In a chorus of long forgotten harmony, And the greatest question is, How can we, how can we really be free From our own arrogance and depravity?

Hello, no one is available to take your call. Please leave a message after the tone. Hey, I hope you're doing okay. I've been sitting here for a while trying to find the right words to say and it's not easy. I guess there's never a good time for a conversation like this, but I didn't want to do it in person because I'm afraid I'm not not able to get through it without breaking down. I want you to know that this isn't easy for me. You mean a lot to me and the last thing I want to do is hurt you. But I also believe in being honest and transparent even when it's painful. I've been doing a lot of thinking lately and it feels like we're both on different paths. Our dreams, our goals, they just seem to be taking us in opposite directions. And as much as it hurts to admit it, I think it's time for both of us to let go. I wish I could pinpoint exactly where things started to change, but it's like the distance between us has been growing and I don't know how to bridge that gap anymore. We used to be so connected, so in sync, but lately it feels like we're becoming strangers. When you understand that this decision doesn't diminish the love and respect I have for you, you deserve someone who can give you the time and attention you need, someone who can share the same dreams and aspirations. I can't be that person right now and I don't want to hold you back. I know it's going to be tough for both of us. We've shared so many beautiful moments and the thought of not having you in my life is incredibly painful. But I also believe that sometimes letting go is the best way to show love and respect for each other. I hope with time we can heal and move forward separately. I wish you all the happiness and success in the world. You deserve it. Please take care of yourself and I hope you find the love and fulfillment you're looking for. I'm sorry for any pain I'm causing and I want you to know that this decision comes from a place of deep reflection and a desire for both of us to find the happiness we deserve. Take care. Thank you.

I'm confident. I'm happy. I'm okay. I'm confident. I'm happy. I'm okay. I'm an island in a dark room. Someone asks how I've been. Offers me a drink, a trip over two words. I'm confident. We both laugh. I'm a fuck up. I don't speak until I have rehearsed things better. I feel my arms crossed. I feel the conversation run off without me. I have failed. Again, I am two blocks away. A girl that's known me 12 years lives on the street that touches mine. I want to ring her doorbell. I want to invite her back to my room with our first bottles of something stolen. I'm matching lies to my mothers. I'm matching outfits always the same size, but I'm afraid she can feel my sweating hands. See the way my jaw locks when I run out of small words that she'll turn and disappear into this silence that I've built. I'm happy. I stay exactly where I am. Scared to turn her to stranger right in front of me. I walk into a room of poets. I shrink down to the size of my shoes. I'm in love with this room and I let it walk all over me. Bow my head whenever a familiar face threatens a smile or a question or room for me to be. I am okay. I repeat this prayer until the death of my own heartbeat is not filling my ears until I'm speaking and not sinking. I am happy until I am shaking and not shaking. I am happy until I am not making the same mistakes every time I break silence, every time I do not forgive myself for being afraid, for being small, for being a puddle disguised as ocean. I'm confident. I'm happy. I'm okay. I repeat these lies ten times a day. My therapist says, if I say them enough, the fear of my own breath will disappear. I will stop trying to cut out my own tongue. I can keep calm and mean it.

My mother taught me this trick. If you repeat something over and over again, it loses its meaning. For example, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, homework, see nothing. Our lives, she said, are the same way. You watch the sunset too often, it just becomes 6 pm. You make the same mistake over and over, you'll stop calling it a mistake. If you just wake up, wake up, wake up, wake up, wake up, wake up, wake up, wake up, one day you'll forget why. Nothing is forever, she said. My parents left each other when I was 7 years old. Before their last argument, they sent me off to the neighbor's house, like some astronaut jettisoned from the shuttle. When I came back, there was no gravity in our home. I imagined it as an accident, though when I left they whispered to each other, I love you. How many times over did they forget what it meant? Family, family, family, family, family, family, family, family, my mother taught me this trick. If you repeat something over and over again, it loses its meaning. This became my favorite game. It made the sting of words evaporate, separation, separation, separation, see nothing apart, apart, apart, apart, apart, see nothing. I'm an injured handyman now. I work with words all day, shut up. I know the irony. When I was young, I was taught that the trick to dominating language was breaking it down, convincing it that it was worthless. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. I love you. See nothing. Soon after my parents' divorce, I developed a stutter. Fate is a cruel and efficient tutor. There is no escape in stutter. You can feel the meaning of every word, drag itself up your throat, separation. Stutter is a cage made of mirrors. Every what do you say? Every just take your time. Every come on, kid, spit it out. There's a glaring reflection of an existence you cannot escape. Every awful moment trips over its own announcement again and again and again until it just hangs there in the center of the room. As of what you had to say, had no gravity at all. Mom, dad, I'm not wasteful with my words anymore. Even now, after hundreds of hours practicing away my stutter, I still feel the claw of meaning in the bottom of my throat. Listen to me. I've heard that even in space, you can hear the scratch of an eye-eye-eye-eye-eye-eye-eye. I love you.

You should stop watching now because this poem will break you, but you won't stop. I know you'll keep watching it. You will sit there, eyes glued to the screen pretending this is just another video, just another string of words, just another person talking into the void. But you know it's not. You know these words taste like your own tears. You know this story sounds too much like yours. You remember when they left, you remember the silence that followed wasn't just quiet. It was violent. It wrapped around your chest and squeezed until you forgot what breathing felt like. Until you started to believe that loneliness was the only thing that never leaves. And grief. No one ever tells you that grief isn't just crying at 2am. It's laughing at a joke and feeling guilty. It's hearing their favorite song and pretending you don't care. It's being okay for three weeks and then breaking down in the middle of the night when you're all alone. And love. No one tells you that love can feel like drowning and heartbreak feels similar to dying. Sometimes you don't miss the person. You miss the way you felt around them. That sometimes the ghosting hurts more than the goodbye because at least a goodbye means they cared enough to end it. And life. No one warns you that growing up feels like losing parts of yourself. That nostalgia is just another word for homesickness. That healing isn't about fixing yourself. It's about learning to live with the cracks. But you won't break. Even though you want to. Even though everything in you is begging for release. Even though the weight of it all makes your bones feel like they are caving in. You won't break. No you shouldn't break. Because you're still here. And you're still watching. And if you're still here, that means you survived the worst day of your life. It means you're stronger than you think. And when this video ends, sit there for a second. Let the silence settle. Let the words sink in. And then, breathe. Take a deep breath. You should stop watching now. Because this poem will break you. But you won't. And you shouldn't.

Oh God, how do I honor you with technology? Oh God, I feel it in my spirit that I owe you an apology. I have scrolled and scrolled, I have judged and judged. But oh God, I can feel it in my spirit. Oh, how I can feel your nudge. Your grace is so insane. My eyes tear up, thinking about it. I am so unworthy. I don't even understand why you bother to continue to pull me out of the pit. Oh God, how do I live fully for you in this technological age? Oh God, humble my heart and give me the courage to step off of the superficial stage. I confess for posting things with selfish motivation. God was even scarier that I often post things mindlessly, ignorantly, not even asking for your confirmation. God, I understand that I have the power not to blend into what's happening around me. Oh God, I realize that everything changed when I was lost, but then you found me. God, I understand that it's not about trolling the lines in the sander, seeing how far I can go without sinning. Oh God, no, my heart knows that as I fix my attention on you, I won't even want that stuff, but realize that you are my filling. Oh God, I ask, how do I not follow the crowd, but still stay relevant? God, I look around through the lens of you and I realize that all of this is so arrogant. I want to be your light. I know that is what my heart screams, but God, this world pulls me in. It messes with my feelings. It messes with my dreams. Oh God, what I think I want to fit into, look pretty to be desired. All of a sudden goes away when in reality, I want everything that I do in my life to be something that makes you smile. Oh God, give me wisdom, give me self control, give me grace. Oh, how I know everything literally changes when I stop scrolling and I look at your face. Create within me a clean heart, oh God. May I rise up in this generation. Create within me a pure mind, oh God. My deepest longing is for every heart to know you, every tribe, every tongue, every nation. Renew a right spirit within me. Make me different. Make me new. Humble, my heart and change me. Oh God, my deepest longing is to really know and reflect you.

I'm okay. You know, there's this thing and it happens quite often. This thing where we'll be asked how we are and our automatic responses. I'm okay. Now sometimes it's true, but other times that I'm okay is covering up the fact that I've had restless nights, breaking moments, worries on top of worries and I hate to say it, even suicidal thoughts. But to you, to a stranger, a teacher, a classmate, a friend, even my mother, I'll say I'm okay. I don't want to be put into this box, into this label, where I'm known as that sad and depressed person when it's to be around. I'll fake a smile if I have to. Lath, be as friendly as possible and act like I know what the hell I'm doing. Maybe if I pretend on those really bad days, I'll start to feel like I'm actually okay. You know, faking until it feels real. It sounds crazy, silly, but we all do it sometimes. I just happen to do it more often than others. Must drop some energy from who knows where and use it in order to function. To keep a conversation going, to feel like I'm not out of place. I feel my heart beating, my chest moving and I know that I'm alive. And yet I sigh. Because I feel like I'm not meeting this quota that I need to fulfill. I'll meet your eyes and give it friendly wave, while inside I feel a horrible weight crushing me down, shaky hands and sporadic thoughts to remind me of all the things I fear. I question. I wonder. I try to avoid. But hey, I'm okay. This one has come up and has given me another day. So I'll play. I'll play the part when it's not really there. Look joyful, full of life. Look like someone that has the world in their hands. I'm okay, is what I'll say. So no one will see the hurricane. That is slowly coming my way.

In something like our mothers we grew, To red was again the color of the water, And pain wasn't something either of us could point to, Because it was what it was, And morning came, not knowing if it would come again, And love was the only thing assumed, And love should have been enough, Someone without a heart might say, The day you died because you wanted to, And tied my wisdom tooth to a doorknob, And pulled it loose, Take everything I think I know, Every answer is a grave. Now the questions are the way I walk through, To find my way to God, And my only God is faith, That there is comfort here, That who is hurting might hurt less than they did before. What else are all these coins, And all these wells for, If not to wish the grief asleep, And the lap of someone else's grief, Not knowing if it will come again, Your sister thought the hearse was a limousine, So she asked what was going, And then she knew for sure, That's what a word like heaven will do, But heaven, that wasn't what you were aiming for, You didn't think the other side would be better, You thought the other side would be nothing at all, Imagine choosing nothing at all, Imagine something hurting them, Not bad, I didn't still have the ring you'd given me, I'd crushed it with a rock to see how much you loved me, I love you to pieces too, It hurts me in my head now, I knew the water was indeed enough to dive into, But I won't let anyone say, It was a shallow thing you did, I knew it was your entire body finally pointing, Saying here, here is where the pain is, I can crush a can with the heal of my shoe, I can drive by your mother's house if I want to, But I don't want to, she was there when you bought the ring, She knew how long you'd been saving me, I didn't save anything, But you don't lose a person like a set of keys, Because you don't find them again, And you can still get to where you're going, Resilience itself is an awful thing to grieve, Who with the heart can stomach, How much we can stomach, All your blood in the water, And I could still wait through, And I will again, And I will again, And I will again, With everyone I lose, So what I want most, What I want most, Is to live the rest of my life, Desperately wanting to live it, I want to give that to you, I want it to find you in the nothing at all, And I want it to be something, When I say, I want to make something of my life, That's what I mean.

Dear best friend, I hope that you're good. I'm glad you're only good. Since you've been gone, it has not been easy. But I want to say thank you. Even though it broke me until a million pieces when you left, I want to say thank you. Even though you miss you every day, I want to say thank you. Thank you for inspiring me, inspiring me to face my fears. You make me want to be better. You make me want to work on myself. And even though doing this without you by my side is one of the hardest things I've ever had to do, I'm doing it. And I wish you could see me. I wish you could be here to see me transform into this new person. But you're not here. I just hope you're proud of me. I'm not mad. I'm just in pain. But what's the sun without a little rain right? I once told you I could conquer the world with just one hand, as long as you were holding the other. Now all I have is the thought of you holding it. But I will still conquer the world, no matter where you are. I will stay strong and stand tall, because I know you wouldn't want to see me fall. Whatever success I'm celebrating, I will always think of you first, because you're my biggest inspiration. And I want you to be proud of me. I just want you to be proud of me. But I want you to keep going too. I want you to win even though I can't be there to celebrate with you. I want you to love yourself. I want you to be yourself. Be the light you want to see in the world. You have everything that you need inside of you. But you know that. I told you more than enough. But I want you to always remember. I hope you remember my words when you feel alone. I hope you remember all the words I told you when you were down on yourself. And I hope you'll find the strength to pick yourself back up if you ever fall. I know you can. I know you will. The person I saw inside of you can handle it all. You're strong. You're intelligent. You're wonderful. You can move mountains if you want to. You should believe in yourself because I believe in you. I know no matter what happens, no matter what you do, no matter where you are in the world, and no matter where I am, I will always love you. And that will never change. Maybe I am the sun and you are the moon. But even they can be seen together in the same sky sometimes. Until we meet again. Take care.

When I die, when my coffin is being taken out, you must never think I am missing this world. Don't fear any tears, don't lament or feel sorry, I am not falling into a monster or service. When you see my corpse has been carried, don't cry for my living. I am not leaving, I am arriving at the dawn of love. When you leave me in the grave, don't say goodbye. Remember, a grave is only a curtain for the paradise behind. You will only see me descending into a grave, now watch me rise. How can there be an end when the sun sets, or the moon goes down? It looks like the end, it seems like a sunset, but in reality it is a dawn. When the grave locks you up, that is when your soul is free. Have you ever seen a seed falling to art, not rise with a new life? Why should you doubt the rise of a seed named human? Have you ever seen a bucket lowered into a well, coming back empty? Why lament for a soul when it can come back like Joseph from the well? When for the last time you close your mouth, your words and so will belong to the world of no place, no time.

14 lines from love letters or suicide notes. One. Don't freak out Two. We both know this has been coming for a long time. Three. I've been staying awake at night, wondering if I should tell you. Four. I bought the kind of crackers you can eat, they are in the hall cupboard. Five. Now that we have watched all the episodes of True Blood, I do not know what else to do next. Six. I always imagined this would happen without warning and like suddenly on a ocean cliff side But this is the kind of thing where waiting for the time to be right, would just mean waiting forever. Seven. I've just been too afraid for too long. Eight. I came home on Tuesday and found all of the chairs that I owned stacked in a tower in the center of my kitchen. I don't know how long they have been like that, but it can only be me that did it. It's the kind of thing a ghost might do to prove to the living that he is still there. I am haunting my own apartment. Nine. My grandmother was still alive when I was five years old and she asked me to check and see if the iron was hot enough yet. So I pressed my hand against it and it was red and screaming for hours. Twenty-five years later she would still sometimes apologize, in the middle of conversations, "I feel so bad about making you touch the iron" she'd say, as though it had just happened. I cannot imagine how we forgive ourselves for all the things we didn't say until it was too late. But how else do you tell if something is hot but to touch it? Ten. I keep imagining my furniture in your apartment. Eleven. I wonder how many likes this will get on Facebook. Twelve. My dad always used to tell the same joke, but I can't remember the punchline. Thirteen. I was eight years old and it took three weeks, three eight-year-old weeks, imagine! To gather everything that I would need to be Batman. Rope. Boomerangs. A Mardi Gras mask with the beads cut off. I couldn't find a cave near my house, so I buried them all in a bundle under the ivy. For years after, I tried to find that spot again. The ivy grew too fast. I searched in so many spots it seemed impossible that I had missed one, but I never found it. How can something be there and then not be there? How do we forgive ourselves for all the things we did not become? Fourteen. I never had the courage to buy bright green sheets. I wanted them but thought they were too brash, even with no one but me to see them. I bought a set yesterday and put them on the bed. I knew that you would like them.

Life moves quietly like a river unbroken, carrying with it the laughter of mornings long past and the soft shadows of evenings heavy with longing. I think of the soldier who sent a letter in 1943. A message meant to bridge distance and fear. Lost time and with it the life he had dreamed. A love held only in the heart. Unseen, unheard, yet burning with silent devotion. I think of two young hearts in Italy. So certain of forever, yet torn apart by silence, by words unsaid by moments stolen by pride, meeting again decades later, only to find the other gone. A life that might have been etched in laughter and touch, now etched in memory, quiet regret. I think of the man who promised his dying wife that he would return to the cafe where their love began, only to avoid it, fearing the weight of absence and grief. And when he finally returned, the walls remembered, the chairs whispered, and he understood that love requires courage. Even when it hurts, even when it is gone. I think of two teenagers, separated by miles and fear, who believed themselves abandoned, though each heart still beat for the other. Years passing, life moving on, and the ache of what might have been, lingering quietly in the spaces between their days. I think of the soldier and his childhood sweetheart. Let us crossing oceans and battlefields. Promises made, promises broken, and the cruel irony of timing. Where one missed word, one lost note could have written a lifetime of joy. Instead, leaving hearts marked with longing and loss. And yet through all this sorrow, through the ache of what was lost, through the shadow of regret, life flows onward, steady and unrelenting, a river that carries both the joy and the pain, the letters, the laughter, the silences, the tears, all mingling in its ceaseless current. So hold your love close, speak the words you feel. Reach across the distance before it becomes forever. Feel the warmth of sunlight and the cleansing rain. For life continues relentless tender. Teaching us that even love that fades, even regret that lingers can carve beauty into our hearts and remind us that every ending, every sorrow, every loss is simply part of the river's flow carrying us toward the next embrace. The next chance, the next echo of what is truly eternal.

I wanted you to see my heart. I wanted you to see through my useless words. I wanted you to see my love. I wanted you to see what I had to offer. I wanted you to see that I wasn't going to just leave you like the others. I wanted you to see what your spell had done to me. I wanted you to see that I could never just up and leave. I wanted you. I wanted you to know that no matter what was said, I would never take anything to heart. Never mind. I did. I took a lot to heart. It was only because I thought every heart you said was pure gold, not for a within. I thought that maybe, just maybe. You'd mean it. I wanted you to know that I loved you everything I could give for my dandy heart. My heart is shattered. I'm broken. To her name too. I thought you could handle me. I thought you could put the pieces back together. That's why I wanted you to. I thought that maybe you'd see past my tiny smile and just bug me and tell me you loved me. If you never did, maybe I was too good at it. I wanted you to see that I wasn't giving up. I wanted you to see that I wasn't giving up on us, on you or on myself. I couldn't. I wanted you. I wanted you to know me like the bag of your hand. I wanted you to be able to spit out facts about me on the spot. I wanted you to say the things that you felt scared to say. I wanted you to know me for me. I wanted you to be able to understand my slight shrugs and my non-dyte hugs. I wanted you to see that I wasn't happy with myself. Sometimes I miss being sick. The grimy is part of me, wishes I had stayed in that familiar city of gray and mental illness and whatever the opposite of healing is. Whether it was nothing to laugh about, but plenty to write about. I've considered myself to be recovered from my eating disorder for three years, but I still write about it in present tense. I also still keep all of my exes in my contact list. And for once, I don't want to write about this. For the first time, I am embarrassed instead of proud of all of the mad things I have done for happiness. When a friend at dinner makes a casual comment on calories, the scoreboard in my head illuminates with numbers again. Once I cut a ribbon the size I wanted to be in order on my waist like a bracelet. Bathroom scales make me feel nostalgic. Like a scrapbook I flip through snapshots of my sickness, the suppers of tobacco smoke and red lipstick. How I used to pack my lunchbox with floss and teeth whitening strips. Last night I painted my nails when I was hungry. I can't eat until the polishes, Jay. I don't want to go into more detail because what if you mistake this poem for an instruction manual? I don't know how to talk about the rabbit hole without accidentally inviting you to follow me down it. And recovery is not all yoga mats and tea and avocados. It is work. It is reminding myself that sucking on ice cubes does not count as dinner. Body forgive me. It is not healthy to drink so much water that your body becomes a bathtub, your organs float in like Lufa's body forgive me. Trying to ignore the caloric calculator in my head is like trying to ignore television subtitles and sometimes I just can't body forgive me. Every is hard work. Not wanting to die is hard work. Every time you ask if I was full I heard you say fat but I am trying so hard not to do that. But I cannot unmemorize the calories of a peppermint. Wanting to die is not the same as wanting to come home. And I am still trying to remember that.

Ugly. What is the definition of ugly? What makes somebody ugly? In a society that tells us how we must look and dress and be, it's easy for someone not in the loop to feel like they aren't free. To the point becomes difficult to even look in the mirror or take a picture for all to see. Well inside we're crying and screaming why me. Glances and comments make us stir and went to hide. It's appearance that matters. Not what's on the inside. How many hours have we spent criticizing our faces, our bodies, every detail that makes us unique? Unique. A word we use to cover up the insecurities and the word society uses to make the odd ones out, not feel so out of place. It feels fake when mostly everyone we see looks and dresses the same. The most beautiful and handsome are the ones who get noticed. It can be a pain. To wonder why we were each giving different qualities and why we can't be like the rest. We hear when makeup is the best, we'll work out routine, we'll trim us down and have people bow at our feet for becoming a part of a cycle that leaves everyone becoming superficial and in need of recognition. In need of hearing words for approval and not of removal. Block hair here, shave there, eliminate wrinkles, don't be so short or too lopsided. We're divided. But not between beautiful and ugly. No. Between confident and low self esteem. Words have a damaging effect when thrown at someone. And those words stick for a lifetime. It should be a crime to lash out words that hurt. But in the end that's just the world we live in, right? Lose your fight? If we could just take a moment in our daily lives to remember that we are all just specks of dust on a planet in a wide universe. Then maybe we won't feel the need to worry so much on how we look. We are all beautiful. So beautiful and we should not let trends in society's norms define us. We can make a fuss, cuss, and complain about what we don't have. But remember, we are who we are and that alone is beauty. Ugly? What is ugly? Perhaps a rotten soul and talks of personality? But you? Ugly? Take a look in the mirror again. Smile. And I'm sure you realize the beauty that is there. The beauty you overlooked. But deep down you knew was always there.

So let me find my counselors and a community struggling just like me. I know you mean to help, but don't belittle our fight to breathe. Help me by being my shoulder to lean, help me by giving me the silence I need, take me to a professional who knows how to heal. You couldn't change a flat tire without tolls your degree. My non-depressed friend, you will love me no doubt to the end of our days, but please don't try to fix me. You don't save people like me this way. Thank you.

The silence after laughter. She once moved through halls where joy would bloom, where sunlight pooled in every room. The walls would hum with voices dear, a symphony she lived to hear. The matron of the hearth, strong and kind, held stories folded deep in mind. But none as sweet as the days they came. Those children, each with a whispered name. They'd tumble in with heart set free, the scent of rain, the taste of glee, with arms that clung and eyes that shone. They brought the world when they came home. Laughter spilled like vintage wine spreading warmth in every line of linen sheets and dinner laid of jokes and games and love replayed. Yet always came that quiet ache. The final night before daybreak. She'd hold her smile, she'd brace her chest and watch them leave with silent unrest. But oh, there were words each promise made were coins of gold that never fade. They'd say cheerfully, optimistically. Soon, we'll come again with light and laughter just like then. She held those vows like sacred thread that tied her to the life ahead. Her faith in joy, her hope in kin, a future bright waiting within. Now silence wraps the house in gray and seasons tip-o, then drift away. She lies in quiet, bound by pain, a soul unspoken yet not in vain. The matren rests though not asleep. Her thoughts swim low, her sorrow deep. She cannot move. She cannot cry, but memories burn behind each eye. She wonders where the voices fled, those whom she raised, whom she once led. Do they recall the songs she sang, the way her arms around them rang? Some still visit when life allows, with weary eyes and furrowed brows. Others lost in distance-wide, working hard just to survive. And still she waits, day after day, for laughter to return and stay. She counts the creeks upon the floor. Imagine faces at the door. The windows weep, the walls don't speak. Her breath grows soft, her bones grow weak. She asks the air faintly, longing, say, where is the dawn? Where are the days I counted on? And then it comes, a hush, a grace, a gentle hand, a once-known face, one figure, tall, now standing near. And all she's held dissolves in tears. No words were said, they weren't required, her weary eyes with truth inspired. A thousand nights of aching plea, now soothed by one familiarity. And as her heart begins to slow, she feels the warmth of long ago. She closes eyes with soul at peace, her waitful filled, her longing ceased. Let it be known that matrons fire never dimmed. She only waited for love to come home again.

alone. How can I describe the feeling of believing that I have no one by my side, when in fact I do? It's strange. You see, I've been singing this song, this song of my life, this song I've had to put on pause rewrite the lyrics to change the temple of, and it feels like I sing it to entertain and soothe the hearts of those around me, of those who love me, just to put their minds at ease and make them think that I'm okay. I'm on this stage trying my hardest to remain here until it's time to complete my performance, but lately I've desperately wanted to end the show. Deep down I feel so alone lost and broken, where it feels like my hope doesn't want to grow. There's a struggle to do basic everyday things and a way on my chest that doesn't want to leave. I'm damaging myself in the process, pushing people away, thinking that they're better off without me and that eventually I'll just rot away. What can I say? I sigh, I cry, I scream, I try, and it feels like my energy doesn't want to recharge, so I'm stuck feeling numb and distant. This isn't a story where I'll be saved. I'm the main protagonist, therefore, the decisions the events and twists rely on me. As I'm writing this with a pen in my hand, I feel a certain power and control I can't seem to grasp on my own. Oh, how I wish I can make the problems, the stress and the worries disappear, remove all of my demons and delete all of my fears. There's some pain every time I listen to a sad song, there's some anger every time I see the nothing that I am, and there's some emptiness that I can't seem to fill, avoid that doesn't want to be covered. Alone, alone, alone, it's even worse because there's no self-love, just me despising myself and everything I do. So I wallow in the sorrow, with little hope of a better tomorrow. Trapped in my mind, dreading the time that beats and hurts me, and the only way out is to stop so I can be free. But more is there to tell, I'm living in my own hell, alone, alone, alone. And maybe as the days go by in the night's drag on, I'll find the strength to continue this tedious and scratch song. Perhaps the smile will remain on my face and stay, allowing me to feel a little less insane. Oh, how I pray. Oh, how I pray.

Hi friends, welcome back to Breath of Poetry in Life. Today's poem is about love, what love can mean and what the absence of love can also mean for somebody. And what it does to the emotions of a person when you need love but you don't have that love in your life. The poem is called Longing for Love. I think love is like letting yourself flow in the stream, like stars with a moon on a clear night, like a rainbow in the sun after rain, like waves in a sea, like snow on a mountain, like hot chocolate on a winter day, like rum on a winter's night, like iced tea on a summer afternoon, like sangria on a summer eve, like an incurable disease. Now knowing what love feels like, I still wonder why I find myself in a stream with no current, like the moon on a cloudy night, without sun after rain, standing in a lake with no waves, atop a heap with no snow. I'm empty bottle of rum on a chilly night, with boiling tea on a scorching day, with no wine, ice and fruits on a sunny eve, immune to the disease of love like a shark. hello all. this has been on my mind a lot and i have no where to go with it, so here i am. my (F24) ex partner (NB, forever 23) died last march. for the sake of this post, i’ll call them Cam (fake name). our relationship spanned from june 2021 until january of 2023 and they were my first love. we broke up for several reasons, one of the main factors being their mental health. they were going through a lot and throughout the relationship i tried to push them to seek help. i supported them in every way i could but my support wasn’t enough and i kept telling them they needed real therapy and/or a psychiatrist. there was only so much i could do. they made small efforts here and there but it ultimately wasn’t enough. it was hard for me to handle their mental health issues along with my own. so for that reason, as well as a few others, we broke up. i heard updates about them occasionally from mutual friends but Cam and i blocked each other on everything. at first we had said we wanted to stay friends but it hurt too much so that didn’t last longer than a couple of days.

Cam reached out to me february 7th, 2024 to tell me that they were in the hospital for a suicide attempt and had been having a lot of medical issues. they said that being in the hospital put a lot into perspective and they wanted to apologize to me. they apologized for the things that went down in our relationship, the way they treated me, and they said if they could do it all over again with everything they knew now, they would in a heartbeat. i apologized as well for my own issues and after a few more messages i sent them a paragraph telling them that i hoped they could find it within themself to just live. to experience the joys in life and try to find purpose and happiness. they blocked me again after that.

in march 2025 my best friend called me while i was in the shower. i answered the phone like i always do when she calls. she asked me what i was doing and i told her i was showering. the tone of her voice told me instantly that something was wrong. she said that she wanted me to hear this from her before i saw anything on social media, and then she told me that my ex had died and she suspected it was from suicide. everything in me shut down in that moment. i couldn’t move i couldn’t speak i couldn’t think. nothing made sense anymore. i knew i had to say something before hanging up so that my best friend didn’t worry about me so i told her id call her back and that i loved her and then i hung up, set my phone on the counter, and stood in the shower long after the water turned cold. i don’t know how long i was in there for. i didn’t cry, not right away. i felt completely and utterly numb.

the crying came the next day. i cried and i sobbed and i was angry and i was heartbroken. i was thousands of miles away, at a multi-week work event. i had no friends or family nearby. i couldn’t attend the funeral, im not sure if i would have anyways. i don’t know if i would have had a place there. i messaged their mom, told her i was sorry for her loss and their family would be in my thoughts. none of my friends or family really seemed to know what to say to me and i cant blame them. there’s no how-to guide on comforting someone who lost their ex partner.

it’s the most confusing grief ive ever experienced in my entire life. it’s not like we were still together, it’s not like we still talked. but i thought of them often. i wished they were doing well. i thought more than once about the possibility of us being the right person, wrong time. i thought about reaching out. but i didnt. we didn’t get back together, we didn’t talk again.

so why is it that now, in june 2026, i still think about them constantly? i find myself mourning for them, for their future, for their family. i see them in everything now. on their birthday my job put me in a hotel on a river walk which held a significance i can’t write in here for privacy reasons. last night i cried over them for the first time in a while and then today my job flew me to a city of which i just discovered that their favorite artist is performing in tonight of all nights. i see them in rainbows and ice cream and texas roadhouse and jeeps and so many other small, simple things. god forbid i listen to the great divide by noah kahan because that just sends me spiraling.

i don’t know what to do with these feelings. i don’t know if im allowed to feel them. we were broken up. we didn’t talk. i don’t know if i have the right to think about them and mourn them. a large part of me feels so much guilt because i couldn’t do or say enough to help them while we were together or when they reached out to me afterwards. but then i wonder if i’m acting too self important to think i could’ve made a difference. and i don’t talk to anyone about these feelings i have because i know that no one knows what to say or how to help and i know that it’s probably weird to even still mourn. i don’t know.

i wish that they had held on. i wish they could’ve lived a long and happy life. i wish i could’ve helped more, pushed more. i wish i had stayed a little bit longer maybe.

maybe im too emotional, too selfish, too dramatic. but i just needed to get this off my chest. in all honesty, and as confusing as these feelings are, i miss them. and i hope they’re doing well, wherever they are. i dont know if theres an afterlife, but for them i hope there is, and i hope they’re much happier there.

It's been a while since you haven't been here, and it feels unreal, I don't even think you're gone like that, I feel like you're on a trip, like you'd visit soon, like one day I'll come home and find you here, using that Goku tank top you liked for some reason.

I remember you died just days before your birthday in December, I was so excited, I had bought you two gifts, one for your birthday, a One Piece Shanks figure because you told me you liked that character, and a Brook one, because I was your secret santa. I remember working and saving up money to buy them fast, just wishing you were getting better, that you wouldn't spend more time in the hospital.

When I heard you were coming back before your birthday, I couldn't hold my excitement and wanted to give you one of the figures as soon as you were home, I even wrote you a "welcome" letter.

I still can't believe my mom made that call that afternoon, the sound of her voice, the shock on everyone's faces, my sister gathering your papers and documents in the living room because well, now we had to prepare your funeral. The ringing in my ears didn't leave me for days, everything was muffled and felt like a dream, even when I saw your face inside that coffin, you didn't even look like yourself, and yet, I had to understand it was you. You were supposed to come home, you were supposed to be here, for your birthday, for Christmas, to receive my gifts, to eat dinner with us, I didn't get to see your smile again, to hug you or even see you, or at least to say goodbye. We were supposed to start our business together remember?, we'd start in your garage and work up from there, I didn't even care if it had that dumb name you chose. 

I still can't believe that night, when we organized everything inside the car for you to lay comfortable so they could get you to the hospital, was the last time I saw you, the last time I hugged you, I wish I hugged you longer, I didn't even get to see your face properly with that oxygen mask, all I saw were your tired eyes looking back at us for a second before getting in the car. Sometimes I overthink about those last moments, did you hug us all because you knew what would happen?, did you say "goodbye" like that for that reason?. 

Now I'm afraid I'm forgetting your face, your voice, your behavior, even your scent, and that makes me so afraid, I don't wanna forget you, I don't want it... Sometimes I beg you at night to please stay in my memories. Pictures and audios cannot hold your essence like memories do. 

I remember you liked the cold weather, you liked anything sweet and hated vegetables. I remember how much you liked One Piece and Superheroes and how you'd force us to watch those long explanation videos or explain way too many things when we asked something simple, how you'd want to collect everything from the shows and characters you liked. How you'd always wear that frayed black coat, or your awful red sneakers I always teased you about, your backpack always hanging from the chair of our dining room, how you'd always forget something when you came to visit and would come back running inside to get it before leaving.

I remember that time as a kid when we watched movies in your room, how you'd hug me on your side, you were so warm, or that time when you dressed up as a werewolf for a party and the mask was awfully funny, you were always so grumpy and yet so lively and fun.

But what scares me the most is how everything is getting... Fuzzy, less and less defined the more time goes by, and my constant memory problems don't help. I'm so afraid I'll forget you as the person you actually were, and only remember you as the idealized and simplified person my mind makes you be. 

I remember your bruised and scarred tissue adobe your forearm veins because of all the medicine you had to take, the amount of times I saw you connected to an IV... Sometimes I wonder how you felt all of those years, how much pain and tiredness you hid under those tired smiles and laughs. Watching you change was painful, I remember my strong brother with a healthy body, slowly swelling, slowly losing his spark, how you'd get tired faster, how you got slower.

Now the only thing I got from you is that drawing you made me on my birthday, I remember teasing you for putting your signature on the back and making it on the backside of a document, but now I cry every time I see it. I used to hate my hands, until you said our hands were similar and that's why we should love them, because it's an undeniable sign we're brothers.

I remember how, from the moment you left, there's an ache in my chest that hasn't gone away, it's there, a dull, small, constant ache, but at the same time, something is missing. Life doesn't feel the same, I don't even know how to describe it, but there's a clear difference from then and now, I can enjoy things, I can be happy, I can smile and feel. But I can't enjoy as much, smile as wide, or be as happy, all of my actions are always tinted by that lingering sensation.

Are you alright?

Do you ever visit us?

Are your health problems gone?

Does your body still aches?

Do you still get cold like you used to?

Do you feel lonely?

I hope your smile is lively now, and not tired like it used to be. You never believed in afterlife of heaven, but I wish with all my heart it is real, because I don't want to think about you as just a decaying body who spent his last years in constant, unending pain and never felt relief.

I miss you. I miss you and love you so much my big brother.

I 32f lost my mom just over a year ago. I had just started my college program in January of 2024, processing a break up and moving back into my mom's place. 3 months later she passed. She was admitted to the hospital in March and passed in April. The cause of her passing was a mixed bag. In the span of 2 weeks she was diagnosed with lung cancer that was already stage 4. It was in her lymph nodes and made its way to her brain. A stroke occurred and everything went downhill fast. 

I'll never forget the phone call from the doctor. I'll remember that night forever. Having to make a choice, do a surgery where there is a 99% chance she will never walk or get out off bed again. She most like wouldn't be herself. Or comfort care. I knew what my mom wanted. ( A little back story, my mom and I helped support my step-dad who had a stroke and became wheelchair bound and a shell of the person he used to be) my mom always told me she didn't want to live like that. To never let her be that way. So on a Friday night where I took time away from visiting my mom in the hospital to try and feel some sort of normal I was at a game night with a new college friend. I was still attending classes and visiting my mom. I was exhausted and doing my best. I got the call and made the decision to move her to comfort care. My world shattered around me in that moment. 

Im the youngest in my family. It was my mom my brother and I after our stepdad passed. My brother was/is going through his own challenges with addiction and that made everything so difficult. Since my brother wasn't really around and flaking out on visits and not answering calls or taking hours to reply. I had to make that decision alone around people I had only meet 4 months prior. 

During my phone call with the doctor she told me "if you have family that wants to say goodbye have them come now" it could be hours or days. So i called my aunts who were 2 and a half hours away in a different city. They drove to the hospital right after our call. My uncle flew in that same night, he got there fast. I smiled too.

I played along.

I acted normal.

Inside I felt like I was being ripped apart.

Later that day she left work early so she could go make the necklace from those charms.

I stayed behind, worked, attended meetings, completed my tasks, went home, opened Hinge and got absolutely nothing.

That contrast broke something inside me.

I asked her out once.

I was so nervous that I couldn't even clearly call it a date.

When she agreed to meet, I was ridiculously excited. I was smiling all night. I was jumping around like an idiot. I tried to look the best I ever had.

All the while there was a voice in my head telling me not to do it.

Telling me she was probably just being polite.

Telling me it wouldn't work.

I ignored it.

The date happened.

I got rejected.

And ever since then I've been replaying every conversation, every interaction, every smile and every moment trying to figure out where I went wrong.

The thing I hate most is that I don't think I'm grieving a relationship.

There was never a relationship.

I'm grieving a future that existed entirely inside my head.

Now every interaction feels like both a gift and a punishment.

The truth is that this isn't only about her.

She just happened to land on top of something that was already there.

I've spent most of my life feeling unwanted.

I was overweight growing up.

Socially anxious.

Didn't have many friends.

Didn't feel like I belonged anywhere.

Didn't feel like I was the guy who got chosen.

Over the last few years I've tried to change that.

I've lost weight.

I've put effort into how I dress.

I've built a skincare routine.

I've tried to become more confident.

I've worked hard on myself in ways that nobody would have imagined if they knew me years ago.

Professionally, my life looks like it should be moving forward.

I'm studying constantly.

I work long hours.

I'm trying to build a startup.

I spend my nights learning new things while other people are relaxing.

The problem is that none of it means anything to me.

People keep telling me to focus on my career.

Focus on my future.

Focus on self-improvement.

Focus on achievements.

I don't know how to explain that none of those things answer the question that keeps me awake at night.

None of those things make me feel wanted.

None of those things make me feel chosen.

I can spend twelve hours working and still come home feeling like my entire day was worthless because nobody actually wants me.

Romantically I've had almost no success.

Recently I downloaded Hinge.

Four weeks.

Zero likes.

Zero matches.

Nothing.

Not one.

And before someone says dating apps don't matter, I understand that.

But when you've spent years trying to improve yourself, years trying to become more attractive, more confident and more presentable, and you still open an app and see absolutely nothing, it starts to feel like you're staring directly at a verdict.

The thing I've realized is that I don't just want a relationship.

I want proof that I'm somebody who can be chosen.

That's the truth underneath all of this.

I want someone to look at me and say:

"Yes. You."

Not because they feel sorry for me.

Not because I convinced them.

Not because I wore them down.

Because they genuinely want me.

And right now I don't know how to live with the possibility that I might never get that.

I (F 22) am about a month out of a 6 year relationship. He (M 21) and I were together since we were 16—we grew into adulthood together. I called him my best friend. I thought we would spend the rest of our lives together, and he would say the same. We spent practically every day together and hardly ever fought, but even if we did, we always worked it out.

I am not naive enough to think that a relationship that began when I barely had my driver's license would last forever. We had different opinions about finances and family and we really didn't actually have that much in common. We most CERTAINLY both had our flaws. I've dealt with anxiety and OCD all my life, as well as chronic migraines and an inflammatory health condition that leaves me bedridden for nearly 1/2 the month. Apparently, my conditions were very tiring for him—and I can understand why. I am not very fun to be around when I'm in excruciating pain for days at a time. But he never told me how much it affected him until he woke me out of a dead sleep to tell me that he was leaving me. He (very unemotionally) laid out all the reasons he was leaving me, mostly to do with finances and how (physically) sick I was. I was so out of it that I didn't even know what to say. He then tried to say he would still like to be friends and didn't want to cut me out of his life forever. I basically was like "ok", and that was the last I saw him.

I handled it exceptionally well. I contemplated what I could have possibly done to deserve such an abrupt end. Unfortunately, there's not really anything I can do about my health. It always made our sex life somewhat difficult, but I had initiated plenty of conversations regarding ways to circumvent that. He was unhappy with the way I handle my money, even though I'm in a very blessed financial position. I still live at home with my parents because they offered to let me stay here while I finish school, and I work 2 part-time jobs, saving the little money I make while earning 2 degrees. He still lives with his dad, but he grew up in an impoverished household with a poor relationship with his family, so I can understand why financial disagreements would be something he couldn't deal with. HOWEVER, during our relationship, he would always say that his career goal was to earn enough money so that I didn't have to work or use my degrees at all. So some mixed signals, I guess. But I can accept that perhaps money may be a good enough reason for us to break up.

It wasn't until after it ended that I realized just how awful he was at communicating about anything. Ever. I never knew how he was feeling or what was going on in his world unless I asked him. If he had any problems, I basically had to beg it out him. He was awful at showing any type of emotion, and if I ever tried to confide in him or get any sort of comfort, I was met with a very stiff unemotional "I'm sorry" or some other lame attempt at care. Don't get me wrong, he showed care through actions—but he just simply could not communicate. That really showed in the way he broke up with me. It was almost...clinical? He said he'd always love me and he hoped that one day we could be friends after listing all the reasons he didn't want to be together anymore, but there wasn't a single emotion on his face. I didn't know it was possible to be so cold.

Anyways, that all leads me to where I am now, a month later. I got my crying over with and moved on with my life. I don't really miss him as much as much as I thought I would. In fact, I kind of resent him, especially for the way things ended. I don't want to be his friend because I don't believe in being friends with exes, and friends should be capable of sharing how they feel with one another. But despite how surprisingly unaffected I've felt by the breakup, the physical toll it's taken on my body is extremely apparent. My anxiety about non-breakup things is tenfold, to the point it's been manifesting physically through heart attack-like symptoms. My inflammation is in overdrive, my health has actually deteriorated rapidly, and I'm definitely depressed. I go to work and come home, watch 4 hours of TV, and then go to bed.

I can't talk to my parents about any of this because they're about as emotionally available as my ex, and kind of the last people I would want any sort of advice from. My friends have all graduated and moved hours away, so I literally have no one in my life right now. I'm so alone. I am already kind of a homebody, and I can't go out to bars and drink because of my stupid health stuff. I don't know how to meet new people, but I really miss having connections with them and hanging out with friends—but how am I supposed to do that? I've never been single or friendless as an adult. I know I'm still so young, but meeting new people and trying again seems like such an impossible task with everything else going on.

I often fantasize about meeting someone who is smart and engaging and capable of expressing how they feel, but then I feel guilty because it's only been a month. How am I supposed to feel? Is it too soon to want to move on? I just want to see this from someone else's point of view so I can figure out where to start.

I don't really know what I'm looking for by posting this. Maybe advice. Maybe perspective. Maybe I just wanted to tell someone.

I need constant talks with people otherwise i break off like tonight

They asked me to feel maybe even write to unravel the pain I hide way deep inside.

But I’m afraid.

Afraid that if I slip into the abyss of my own making not even poetry can save me.

But maybe that’s what I need absolution before solutions.

So here it is, in plain and white.

But no today I won’t speak of the one who recently shattered my heart.

Not today.

Today, I want to talk of something else.

Something more.

One month.

That’s all we get.

Thirty days to feel, before we go back to shrinking, back to holding in our tears like our fathers taught us and their fathers before them.

I look around with the same eyes my father had.

Never really saw the struggle he tucked behind his smile but sometimes it slipped, just a flicker.

Too painful to ignore, too human to hide.

I wonder how much he held in before going back to our Father.

I wonder how many men carried wars inside them with no medals to show for it.

How many dreams were buried next to the boy they silenced just to survive?!

I’ve seen too many of us put flowers in empty vases hoping beauty might fill the hollow.

We say “I’m good” with cracked voices and trembling hands, because honesty still feels like weakness in a world that only applauds composure.

But I’ve learned we don’t die when breath leaves the body.

We die when the inner child goes quiet, and we keep walking around like museums of pain no one visits.

A generation of ghosts, men who were taught to stay silent, even when it killed them.

A lineage of locked jaws and swallowed grief passed down like wedding rings, but heavier.

A history of hands that built homes but never held their sons of eyes that watched, but never wept.

A cycle that praised survival and punished softness, that told us “strong” means “alone.”

But I stand here now—spine crooked from the weight with the chance to choose differently.

To be the fracture in the pattern.

The first whisper after centuries of silence and maybe that’s what this month should’ve been.

Not a performance, not a box ticked, but a reckoning.

A remembering.

That men cry too.

That we feel.

That we fall apart.

And that healing starts not in noise but in the quiet confession,

“I need help.”

So here it is.

Not for applause.

Not for pity.

But maybe for the boy still inside me

who just wanted to be seen and told

“You don’t have to carry all of this alone.”

And I won’t lie it’s hard being a man right now.

Not because we’re the victims but because sometimes it feels like no one believes we can be.

I see the tweets.

“Men are trash.”

“Fear men.”

And it’s not that I don’t get it.

It’s not that I don’t know some of us carry knives where hearts should be but what happens to the rest of us?!

The ones trying to build not break?!

The ones who are still learning but showing up anyway?!

What happens when we become guilty by association and our love is weighed against

our wallets?!

When “being there” isn’t enough unless there’s a transaction?!

I talked to a girl yesterday.

She asked me to send her money to braid her hair and maybe that’s normal now.

But it made me pause.

Because I didn’t even know her like that.

And I wondered when did love become an invoice?!

When did affection start coming with terms and conditions?!

We talk about red flags, but sometimes I wonder

if we’re even trying to build or just competing to not be the one who gets hurt first.

It’s not an attack.

This isn’t bitterness dressed in verse.

It’s just a sigh.

A tired breath from a man who’s trying to love better, to be better, to unlearn what broke his father and still feel like he’s being seen through a lens he didn’t ask for.

My relationship with my father it was complicated.

Towards the end, we found some understanding but it was heavy with expectation.

Not because he didn’t believe in me but maybe because he believed too much, in ways I couldn’t reach.

I wasn’t always the son he imagined, the version of “good” he saw in his head.

And maybe that’s the quiet story of so many of us men trying to live up to a shadow while we’re still figuring out how to stand in our own light.

I look around and I see the same struggle echoed friends who never had a straight line with their fathers, or worse, no line at all.

For us men, that absence sometimes feels like a map without a legend.

Fathers who didn’t hug or didn’t know how to say they loved us.

Husbands caught between being providers and feeling present sometimes losing both roles in the noise of what’s expected.

And what about being role models?!

We want to show strength but strength isn’t just muscle or money it’s vulnerability, too.

It’s saying “I don’t know,” and meaning it.

It’s teaching the boys who watch us that it’s okay to bleed, to ask for help, to be human.

Because if we don’t break the cycle, who will?!

This is why I was afraid because one line opens another, like Pandora’s box stretching infinite across time.

Chains we once carried, even after we were set free, our minds remained shackled and our hearts once loved and shattered chose to cage themselves in safe little corners.

Because heartbreak can tip you over to the other side.

I’m not saying we’re great hell, sometimes I can’t even convince myself of that but damn, sometimes we carry so much pain, hold so many silent storms inside, that if we all dared to open up our minds, the world would wonder, how we manage not to break.

How we don’t go mad.

Maybe that’s the real weight not the battles we fight out loud but the quiet wars inside these chests, the bruises no one sees, the nights we don’t sleep, the prayers whispered when no one’s listening and the tears we swallow because showing them feels like defeat.

But here we are still breathing, still fighting, still trying to be something better than what was handed down.

And maybe that’s enough for now.

One month.

30 days.

4 weeks.

Then what?!

Suddenly, all the concerns I had originally raised and she had dismissed became her concerns. She said that in person she noticed my older appearance more, and that it made her question whether being with me really made sense. She also suddenly became worried about how her family would react. She wasn’t concerned about her mother, but she said it would still feel strange bringing me home to meet them (her father isn’t around, only her stepfather). On top of that, she said she wants to get married within the next five years and is looking for the perfect partner, someone who feels like a perfect match both inside and outside. She said she doesn’t want someone whose appearance only “half fits,” even though she thinks I’m a great person who treats her well and fits perfect for what she looks for in an partner. despite the fact that she feels a strong emotional connection with me and can open up to me in ways she can’t with anyone else, she can't imagine marrying someone who isn't a perfect physical match for her.

After the meeting, I was already somewhat attached. Four days full of happiness, affection, and physical closeness don’t leave me unaffected. So I tried to reassure her and address her concerns.

After about two days of going back and forth, she lied to me. She told me she was going to stay overnight at a female friend’s place. The next day, she messaged me saying she didn’t think there was a future for us and that she wouldn’t be able to develop romantic feelings for me. After talking more, she confessed since she felt guilty, that she had actually wants to met up with her ex-boyfriend. They had been together for 1.5 years and had been broken up for seven months. According to her, it was only as friends, but she also said she would sleep in the same bed and cuddle with him.

To define “casual”: we are both allowed to meet new people, but if things start becoming serious with someone else, I want us to end whatever we have, because I can’t handle the idea of her dating or beeing physical with other guys. It’s already hard enough for me to accept that she still wants to see her ex from time to time.

I have the feeling she hasn’t fully let go of her ex, which is why she still wants him in her life. She says she doesn’t want to get to know anyone else right now. The reason was that she felt he was still very immature, which is why she no longer saw a future with him. But she would consider getting back together with him if he became more mature. Sshe would end thing with him, when she finds someone that she is 100% of she can have a realtionship with.

I’m probably only agreeing to this because I still hope she’ll eventually develop feelings and decide she wants a relationship. Maybe that’s just delusional wishful thinking, but letting go is hard. I've known this guy my whole life, I am very close with his family and him with mine. We lived together for multiple years.

A few years ago, my friend (lets call him Alex) and my sister decided to try and date. We all grew up together and were all close throughout childhood. Both of our families were supportive of the match, for years we had talked about the two of them possibly ending up together and they finally decided to give it a shot (there is a bit more to that story, but it's relatively irrelevant to this post). For added context, I lived with Alex at the time in our hometown, my sister lived about two hours away so there was distance involved.

After a few dates, my sister realized that this relationship wasn't what she wanted for various reasons and she called it quits. Alex was pretty beat up about it, he was already 100% invested at this point and already had been thinking about their future together. It was pretty unfortunate, but my sister had every right to put a pause on things when she did. She thought she had feelings for him, but basically realized they did not have the romantic chemistry she was looking for. I was there for Alex though, after all we lived together at the time. I talked to him a lot about the situation and he didn't seem to view me any differently at the time as we had been friends for so long. We remained close at the time, but eventually my life circumstances changed and I ended up moving out of that house. We remained in touch and I still talked with him and hung out with him frequently.

Fast forward to about a year ago. My friend Alex meets a new girl through his work and hits it off with her. I hadn't met her, but was happy for him. It's his first time dating someone new since he had dated my sister briefly. For additional context, Alex also has a job that makes him immensely more busy during the summer time. So, he starts dating this girl at the beginning of summer and between her and work, he has no free time so I go several months without seeing him in person, but every so often he hops on our friend's Discord so I know he's doing okay. Going into the fall, I expect he might be able to hang out again, but unfortunately he is harder to reach then ever. I asked his family if he was doing okay, they say he is doing good, just busy with his new girlfriend so they hardly see him too. I also learn that him and his new girlfriend are moving in together despite only being together a few months.

I don't hear from him at all until the week of Thanksgiving. A couple days before the holiday, he just sends me a picture of a few totes of mine that were in his garage still, basically saying "can you come get these? or if you don't have time I can just take them to the dump", I feel kinda bad because I should've remembered I still had those there (they were just keepsakes, nothing I really needed), but at the same time I was also letting him use several pieces of my furniture in his house as well, so I felt like it wasn't a big deal if I had some stuff in the garage. Anyways, I tell him I have time on Thanksgiving to come grab that stuff. At about noon on Thanksgiving, I show up to his house to collect my things and expect to be greeted by Alex. Instead, I am let in the house by his little brother (who had taken my room a while after I had moved out, so it wasn't like a big shock). He lets me know Alex and his girlfriend were still sleeping in their room, so I wouldn't be seeing them. I collect my things and go, I also had some stuff I threw away in his trash, so I texted him to let him know I used his trash can outside, he said thanks for letting him know and we left it at that.

Fast forward to the beginning of this year, I hear through my family that Alex is now engaged and they are getting married in May. I text him congratulations, he says thanks. I am tempted to ask about details, but at that point I haven't had a conversation with him in over half a year so I decide to wait until I get a wedding invite to ask him about it. Even though we hadn't been in contact for a while, I was still hopeful he might ask me to be a groomsman, it was something we had always talked about. But either way I'm sure I will at least be getting an invite to the wedding... A couple months later, I learn from his family that there will be no groomsmen, Alex's fiancé didn't really have any friends to be bridesmaids so it wouldn't make sense for there to be groomsmen.... Right, gotcha. A bit after that is when I learn the best part: Myself and none of my family was invited to attend the wedding. Reason being "it would be awkward if his Ex's family was there"...

Like I had said, our two families are as tight as I've ever seen two familes be. Our moms were best friends, I've known all of them since I was born, and same goes for him and my family. It was a massive shock to us and genuinely upsetting for us and for his family, but they don't want to alienate him so they don't protest to his decision. My sister was very distraught about the whole situation because she thought it was all her fault, I reassure her it is absolutely not her fault, and fuck Alex if he has decided he doesn't want us in his life anymore.

Fast forward to today, it's been a few weeks since the wedding. It's still very much the main talking point between out two families, everyone is still quite upset about it.
