Back in 2016/17 I became best friends with someone online. We played games together, watched movies and TV shows constantly, had the same favourite bands, and talked every day.

In 2018 we finally met in person and admitted we had feelings for each other. It was my first relationship and I was already 23. We then spent years doing long distance, getting through COVID and visiting each other whenever we could.

In 2023 I made a huge leap and moved across the world to be with her. We had spent years waiting for that moment and I thought we were finally starting the life we'd always talked about.

I'm not perfect. I have anxiety and a tendency to avoid difficult conversations. Looking back, I can also see that I wasn't fully honest with myself about how homesick I was going to be, how difficult immigrating would feel, or how much being closeted was affecting me. I wasn't out to my family when I moved there, which in hindsight I deeply regret.

The problem is that from almost the moment I arrived, she seemed unhappy. There were frequent conversations about how I had misrepresented my intentions by moving there, that I wasn't fully committed, and that I wasn't building a future together in the way she expected.

Those criticisms were fair. I had never lived independently before. I wasn't great at domestic life. I was hesitant about spending large amounts of money furnishing an apartment when I was still trying to process such a huge life change. I can absolutely see how that would have been frustrating.

At the same time, I felt increasingly deflated. I had left my entire life behind to be there, was struggling with homesickness, wasn't out to my family, and at one point was having near-daily nightmares from the stress. We also both lived and worked in the same 2 bedroom, spending literally 24 hours a day together (it was too much).

Despite all of that, we were still best friends and there were good times too.

Then the incident happened that she has never been able to move past.

She had vacation time planned from work and we wanted to take a trip together. Around the same time, my family started discussing coming to visit because I hadn't seen them in nearly a year and my visa situation meant I might not have much longer left in the country.

The scheduling became complicated because my parents, sisters, and my partner all had limited availability that ended up overlapping.

I wanted everyone to come. I told my family that I wanted her included. My family also knew her and liked her from previous visits, although they didn't fully understand the nature of our relationship because I wasn't out.

At one point my parents suggested a compromise to me. It was a roughly two-week trip, and because my partner had already been to one of the destinations before, they wondered whether she might be open to heading back a few days earlier than the rest of us. Their thinking was that we'd have time together, they'd have some family time with me, and we'd all still spend most of the trip together.

I knew it was an awkward suggestion. I also knew there was a risk it would come across badly and I was scared of the reaction. But instead of properly managing the situation myself, I brought it up.

She was understandably hurt and interpreted it as my family not wanting her there.

My parents were horrified when they realised how upset she was. My dad sent her a message explaining the misunderstanding and saying she had always been good to me and that they would be happy to have her there. He wasn't trying to exclude her.

Unfortunately things escalated from there. She sent long messages (to my dad and sister) analysing my family dynamics, suggesting family members needed therapy, and making judgments about people she didn't know particularly well. My dad didn't engage with those accusations and the issue was never really resolved.

I also came out to my family during that trip. Part of the reason was that I became frightened by how serious everything had become and felt I could no longer keep hiding such a huge part of my life. I also based on a phonecall thought she was insinuating she had outed me in said messages, and when I started freaking out she wouldn't pick up or answer my call back.

The trip itself ended up being okay, but the argument never really died.

For the last year it has been revisited again and again. I've apologised repeatedly for my role in it. I've acknowledged that I handled it badly. I've explained my thinking, my family's thinking, and the context around it more times than I can count. It was my fault.

We basically unofficially broke up because of that, but remained living together until my visa expired in December. Then I moved home. I initially had more boundaries, not spending long nights talking on the phone as much, no endless gaming. More time working on my own things. But still checking in and talking when we needed each other, because again I care about her and she had some really hard things going on. I guess that's increased slightly more over the last few weeks and months. But still I felt like I had some distance.

Over the last month the trip has been brought up again in detail. I was being asked why every person said what they said, what everyone's motives were, and was told that my family was manipulative, awful, or worse.

Eventually I was being pressured to call my family immediately so they could answer questions directly. I became so stressed that I ended up taking a beta blocker just to calm down.

I eventually called my dad and explained the situation. From his perspective this was a misunderstanding from a year ago that had already been discussed many times.

Even that wasn't enough. More family members needed to be involved. More questions needed answering.

At that point I finally said I wasn't comfortable bringing my family into the middle of it again.

That appears to have ended things completely. She said bye yesterday and that was it. We're not even friends anymore.

I know I made mistakes. I know I handled parts of this badly. I know my avoidance contributed to the original problem.

What I genuinely don't know anymore is whether this is a normal consequence of my actions, or whether I've spent a year trying to fix something that was never actually fixable.

My work has suffered. I can't focus. I feel guilty constantly. I feel like I've apologised for the same mistake hundreds of times and somehow we're still exactly where we started.

I'm not looking to be told I'm perfect or that she's entirely wrong. I just want honest outside perspectives because I feel completely lost.

My boyfriend and I have been together since 2023. We met on Hinge, and for a long time I really felt like he was my person. I still love him, and I still want a future with him, which is what makes this so hard.

Our relationship has had a lot of ups and downs. There was cheating/broken trust in the past, and we ended up taking a break. During that time, there were confusing boundaries and “just friends” type rules that made me feel like he was pulling away instead of fighting for us. We eventually tried to work through it, and we have gone to therapy together. I do think some things have improved, and we have worked through some toxic patterns better than before.

But I still feel like I’m carrying a lot from our past, and the present keeps triggering those feelings.

I have an anxious attachment style, and he is more avoidant. That has created a push-pull dynamic where I need reassurance, communication, and emotional closeness, while he sometimes shuts down or acts like I’m asking for too much. When I bring things up, I sometimes feel like I have to explain why something hurt me instead of feeling like he naturally wants to understand.

On top of that, we went through a pregnancy/loss situation, and that changed me emotionally and physically. I feel like my body and heart went through something major, and I don’t always feel like he fully understands how fragile and disconnected that left me feeling. Since then, reassurance, emotional safety, and intimacy feel even more important to me.

One of the biggest issues right now is our sex life and lack of deeper intimacy. We usually have sex about once a week, but mostly only on weekends or days when we are both free. It is usually quick, maybe around 10 to 15 minutes, and I do not always finish.

It is not that I have an issue finishing. I know my body, and I know I am capable of that. But when my insecurities start popping up, or when I feel pressure to finish quickly, it makes it harder. Then I start feeling bad, like I am doing something wrong by not finishing in the amount of time he gives me. It puts more pressure on me, and then I cannot fully relax into it.

The hard part is that I miss feeling wanted, desired, and deeply connected. I find myself dwelling on my very far past sometimes because I used to be way more intimate with other people. Not just physically, but emotionally too. I miss feeling explored, wanted, and connected. I want that with him so badly, but sometimes I feel like he does not let that kind of connection happen.

I have started making up fantasies in my head because it feels like there is a part of me that is not being reached. I do try to relieve myself, but that is not really what I am looking for. It is not just about release. It is about connection, passion, feeling chosen, and feeling like my partner actually wants to be close to me.

I also feel like the intimacy issue is connected to a bigger unmet need in the relationship. I keep asking for deeper commitment, reassurance, and signs that he is serious about our future. I have asked for a ring. He has said we should get a house first, and I understand that a house is a big future goal. We both agreed that a promise ring could be a good placeholder until then.

But it hurts when I see him spend thousands of dollars on his hobbies while the ring for me keeps feeling pushed aside. To me, it is not just about jewelry. It is about feeling prioritized. It makes me question why the things he wants can happen, but something that would mean a lot to me emotionally keeps getting delayed.

Sometimes I feel like he can be selfish. I feel like his wants, comfort, hobbies, and timeline come first, while my emotional needs are treated like pressure or nagging. I do not want to force someone to commit to me, but I also do not want to feel like I am begging for signs that I matter.

At the same time, I want to be fair. He is not all bad. He can be a gentleman. He does take me on small dates sometimes, we go to dinners, he helps clean, and he does take care of most of the things that are his responsibilities. There are good parts of him and good parts of our relationship. That is why this is confusing.

I feel like I am only saying the bad things, but I am pointing them out because they are the things sitting on my mind. The good things are real, but the painful things are starting to feel louder.

I do not want to make the whole relationship about sex, a ring, or the past. But all of it together makes me feel like I am missing something important: emotional safety, passion, commitment, and feeling truly chosen.

I don’t want to punish him forever for the past. I know people can grow. I also know relationships take work, and I am not trying to pretend I’m perfect either. I can be emotional, sensitive, and I know my anxious attachment can make me need more reassurance than some people. But I also don’t want to shrink my needs just to keep the relationship.

I feel torn because I do love him. I do want a future with him. We have had better moments, and I know we have both tried in different ways. But I’m scared that I’m holding onto the potential of what we could be instead of accepting what the relationship actually feels like right now.

Has anyone stayed after broken trust and actually rebuilt a healthy relationship? How did you know the difference between normal healing taking time versus realizing the relationship was still hurting you?

Also, for anyone who has dealt with low intimacy, feeling deprioritized, or wanting more commitment from a partner who says they want a future but does not always show it in the ways you need, did it get better?

I’m not asking Reddit to make the decision for me. I just want outside perspectives because I feel stuck between loving him, wanting our future, and wondering if I’m ignoring how much pain I’m still in.

I (22NB) just finished my undergrad in the arts*. My field of study involves an enormous amount of 1:1 time with professors, and people often train this way for years before even getting to college, so I've been on the receiving end of many hours of this kind of teaching. At this school, I had a lot of experiences that were fine but never stuck with me, until I met my dear mentor (76M). In my first lesson with him, he looked me in the eye for maybe thirty seconds, and then asked me what I thought about Prometheus's original sin, and why it was such a monumental event. Mind you, I was ostensibly to study advanced musicality with this man. I, being who I am, must have answered decently enough, because he seemed impressed and we had a good conversation.

Some context - I've felt extremely different and isolated from most people I've met throughout my life, even my really wonderful and supportive parents. I'm not sure how to articulate why, but I think I experience life in a fundamentally different way (although of course I have no way of really knowing). Lots of people have given me labels to understand this feeling: gifted, neurodivergent, autistic, odd, weird, etc. It's taken me quite a few years of therapy to accept that I'll always feel a little bit like this, and the people that make me feel safe to just be myself are the ones worth keeping around. This is why I ended up going to art school, to try and connect with myself and maybe connect with others while doing so. It's helped a bit.

What was different about this mentor is I could tell from his first looking over of me that this is a man who could read me instantly and actually understood everything he needed in that instant as well. I know it's a trope, but I really do feel like he x-rayed me and saw what I needed and that he could help me. I also knew pretty quickly that I was in the presence of a real genius, not the self-important kind that drinks their own Kool-Aid, but an actual genius, the scale of which I was barely able to comprehend. As a byproduct of being labeled "Gifted" when I was a kid, I haven't met very many people that really make me feel like I know nothing (in a good way), but this guy is at the top of the list. What began as a routine exercise in musical improvisation would routinely go off the rails into Greek mythology, evolution, the human mind, the human condition, a religious painting, etymology, and so many other things I never could have imagined. When he spoke, he had me in the palm of his hand and I felt like he could open entire worlds up to me in a way no one else ever has.

In my first year studying with him, he was still very much "in the woodwork" as he called it at our school. He'd been department chair multiple decades ago, but quit after an extremely frustrating setback in changing our admittedly extremely backward-looking curriculum into something more fit for creatives in the 20th/21st centuries. As a result of this quitting, he had more or less free rein to teach whatever he wanted, and whomever he wanted. He would take basically everyone that came to him, but they had to come to him by themselves - he never recruited anyone. I understand that this made those of us he chose feel special maybe without merit, but I never felt special because he chose me - I felt it because he really saw me. Our lessons would be scheduled by the school for 90 minutes. In my lessons, he would routinely teach me for almost three hours, to the point where I had to make sure that he knew what time it was so he wouldn't miss anything.

In my second year with him, there was a pretty massive shakeup at school and one thing led to another and he became department chair again. This on paper was a great thing - he could make the curriculum changes he'd wanted and make things better for everyone. I should have seen the writing on the wall then. Now is a good time to say that he was not exactly a beacon of physical stability. His skin was pretty fragile and thin, and he barely ate two full meals a day and had trouble sleeping because his mind wouldn't stop racing. More than anyone I know, he was also afflicted with various strange maladies, that would pop up one after another and then disappear without explanation. To make an extremely long story short, over the course of this year he realized he was no longer as young as he used to be and his health became quite poor to the point where he finished out the year in the hospital, no longer able to teach. I think the last time he actually was in the school building was to see my senior capstone, which I'll be kicking myself over forever.

I visited him in the hospital before graduation, and that made me understand why people want to go quickly and peacefully. He was clearly not well, but trying to stay optimistic. He did get well enough to be discharged and travel back to his country home with his wife, but was hospitalized again with some illness and died a few days later.

I was on a school trip out of state when I got the call - thankfully I was in my hotel room because I lost it pretty bad. I called my partner, then my mother, then my best friend (who was the one to tell me), and had trouble getting more than a few words out because I was crying so hard. Later that day, I had to face my schoolmates, who all knew him and had a very different experience of him than I did, and I felt like a zoo animal because it was not a secret how much he believed in me and the relationship we had. I don't even know why I'm writing all this detail, but some part of me thinks it's important.

It's been about a month now since he died and I'm really not doing much better than that first day. Everyone's been asking me if I'm okay and I've gotten better at pretending, but I just feel so lost and really sad. I know he was 'just my professor', but we had a personal relationship as well, and I was supposed to be his TA/co-teacher next year after I graduated and now I'm just left with this huge hole and huge sense of responsibility to make sense of his writing and try to transmit his insane theory of music in some meaningful way.

At least once a semester, he would tell all of his chosen ones in our weekly seminar that he loved us all, even though he wasn't supposed to say that, but he really did, because we gave him the hope and the energy to stay curious. I loved him too, because he made me feel like there was no shame in keeping my childlike wonder alive and allowing myself to be overtaken by emotion in the face of humanity. I don't know how I'll go the entire rest of my life without talking to him ever again. I feel like there are some people we are destined to meet, and I felt that when I met him. I guess this moment was inevitable, but I didn't think it would come so soon and I'm just really overwhelmed by grief and don't know what to do. I've written all this because I loved him so much and I'm afraid he died not knowing how much I cared about him, and because I would give almost anything to have one last afternoon with him.

On August 23rd at 4:45 my best friend and first love passed away. He was only 19. So young. I met him back in high school. 10th grade. I remember when I first saw him and how lonely he looked. I felt bad for him because I too understood being lonely, having no friends and being new. Somehow along the line we began talking, our seats got moved next to each other and we clicked. We’d joke around and talk. He’d let me play in his hair. He was so so so funny. I realized then that I had developed feelings for him. I’d write about him in my journal and at some point he’d started reading my journal as well. I wrote him a letter and had decided to give it to him the last day of school. I think he knew I liked him. I had told him that I’d liked this guy and I was scared to tell him. He didn’t end up getting that letter until the next school year. 11th grade was more so of us getting closer. He wanted to be with me but I have strict parents and I’d told him no. He ended up dating another girl, I was devastated. They broke up like almost a month later. He told me he still liked me and that she wasn’t me. We grew closer and ended up getting together. That experience was so new and fresh. He was so sweet. Flowers, candy and gifts. Holding hands. I remember our first kiss, our first hug. Late nights on zoom because of the fact that my strict parents wouldn’t let me have a phone. It quickly turned to hell when my parents found out and had to get “disciplined”. We still stayed together but it was hard especially when we couldn’t talk outside of school. We broke up that summer. Senior year was so messy with us. He wanted to try again and I did too but didn’t want to deal with my parents and getting kicked out like I had almost been that summer. I don’t know what happened but we started texting again and shared a kiss and after that we were back to how we were before. It was so fun. Secret kisses, hugs, letters, late night calls. Spending time in class and on the game together. Always together. Until he started getting sick. He would come to school coughing and sick. Until he just didn’t show up. He told me it was just a cold and then he told me it was strep throat but he kept getting worse until a late night hospital visit where they told him he had cancer. Leukemia. For 3 months he was on a ventilator fighting for his life. Fluid in his lungs and worse. I’d call everyday and talk to his mom and I really thought he was going to die. I’d told my mom about him and she didn’t really seem to care. I never got to visit him. He got better though and when they let him out for 2 weeks I got to see him. I think it was July. He had lost so much weight. We hugged and kissed. We called everyday night and talked. For the next few months he was in and out the hospital until they let him go home. I was so happy for him. He would come visit me at my job, we’d hang out on my breaks. I remember for his last birthday, April 13th we had a sort of picnic thingy. We laid a blanket in an open field and listened to music ate food, talked and he held me. The very last time we hung out together was at his house. I’d pretended to go to work and changed in an uber. It was for my birthday. I’d never been to a guys house before and it was all so new. I just remember looking around and just in shock. The room I always wanted to go to and look at. The bed I always wanted to sleep in, cuddle in. We watched tv, listened to music, cuddled, napped together. I remember laying my head on his chest and just him breathing. His mom drove me half way home and then he walked with me. I gave him a hug and kissed him goodbye. That was the last time we were together in person wise. A few days later at his check up he was diagnosed with cancer again and wasn’t allowed to leave the hospital. I called and texted but idk what happened between then and now. I became so focused on work and I just thought he’d be fine. I needed to work more so I could get a car and go see him like we’d talked about. I wasn’t calling as much but I would text and see how he was. Send him reels and dumb stuff like that. He’d told me he’d felt neglected and wanted me to call more. So I did. I’d text, call but it was hard. Working so many hours, watching my siblings, cooking, cleaning. He’d stopped answering the calls. He was so tired and sick. The very last message I have from him was August 16th. I couldn’t even respond because I had screen time on my phone. When I did respond I guess it was too late. I think I’d called him the Friday before the 16th. Which was our last phone call. I asked if I woke him up and He’d told me yes and that he was tired and I asked him if he’d wanted to talk later. He said yes and i never heard from him after. I decided to text his mom and apologize because she was upset with me. She never responded so I left her alone. I called his phone, texted him, the whole two weeks. I found out on the 22nd he was on dialysis and wasn’t doing good. I found out through a friend who saw his stepdads Facebook post. I couldn’t even call because of screen time. I prayed for him and sent him a message on instagram the next day. He died an hour after I’d texted him. I was in church when I’d found out and my parents wouldn’t even let me leave. I texted both of his parents and neither responded. I called her two days later after trying to decide whether I should or not. She chewed me up and so did his stepdad. To make it worse I wasn’t able to make it to his viewing or funeral because my parents found out and yelled and screamed at me. Telling me no, I was told it was my fault for getting emotionally invested in him. Of course his mom was pissed and refused to understand. I just made this post to share the story I had with him and I hope that if you have someone special in your life that you cherish them. Life is so full of unexpected things.

I am posting this because I want objective opinions on a situation that has affected my life for months. I am not looking for revenge. I am trying to understand whether my expectations were unreasonable and how other people would view what happened.

I am from India, and I think that cultural context is important. In many Indian families, an unplanned pregnancy and abortion are not just private medical events. They carry significant emotional, social and family consequences, especially for women. This is one of the reasons why I felt trapped throughout the entire situation.

My ex and I were in a relationship for almost five years and were both enrolled in an executive program at IIM Indore.

By October, our relationship was already struggling.

On 11th October, we had sex. I initially did not want to have unprotected sex because I was worried about the consequences. He insisted, and I eventually agreed. Looking back, I know it was my decision in the end, but one of the reasons I agreed was because our relationship was on the verge of ending and I genuinely believed intimacy might help us reconnect.

On 12th October, he left for Diwali.

What I did not know at the time was that he had effectively moved out and shifted his life to Bangalore.

The practical impact of this was immediate. I suddenly found myself having to manage everything on my own. I had to handle rent, household expenses and other day-to-day responsibilities by myself. There was no discussion, planning or transition. I simply found myself dealing with the financial burden alone while also trying to understand what was happening to the relationship.

A few weeks later, I found out that I was pregnant.

When I informed him, he told me that I was making it up to stop him from leaving. From that point onwards, I felt that most conversations revolved around proving that the pregnancy was fake rather than discussing the situation itself.

He blocked me on all communication channels. The only way I could contact him was through GPay messages.

Since we were both studying in the same college program, I reached out to some of his friends because I was unable to communicate with him directly. My intention was not to create drama. I was hoping someone could make him understand the seriousness of the situation and encourage him to have a conversation with me.

At that point, I was dealing with the pregnancy largely on my own.

Eventually, I took abortion pills without proper medical consultation.

Looking back, I understand that this was not the right way to handle it, but at the time I felt overwhelmed, unsupported and completely lost.

I went through the abortion process largely alone.

After taking the pills, I asked him if I could come to Bangalore because I was finding it difficult to stay at home after the abortion. I wanted a place where I could recover physically and mentally.

I went to Bangalore and stayed with him for a short period.

During that time, there was an argument in which I felt physically pushed. He also refused to share a bed with me despite us having been together for almost five years. I understand that nobody is obligated to provide affection after a relationship has ended, but from my perspective it reinforced the feeling that I was completely unwelcome there.

I also came to know that he had told his flatmate that my pregnancy was fake.

Imagine going through a pregnancy and abortion and then finding out that the entire situation is being spoken about as if it never happened.

Eventually, he left the apartment and I left as well. I moved to a friend's place in Bangalore because I did not have anywhere else to stay.

During this period, I contacted a women's support cell seeking guidance. However, I never filed a formal complaint because I still hoped that things could be resolved through communication.

After returning, I tried to move on.

However, my health did not feel normal afterwards. I did not get my periods until March and assumed it was related to taking abortion medication, although I remained concerned about my health.

In February, both of us attended a residency at IIM Indore as part of our executive program.

Seeing him again brought back everything that had happened over the previous months.

By that point, I was struggling mentally and emotionally to an extent that I had never experienced before. I repeatedly told him that I was not coping well and that I was having thoughts of not wanting to continue living.

At one point, he called me to his room.

I hoped we would finally have a conversation about everything that had happened.  
But he just pushed me away even that time.

I had also specifically requested that he not discuss our relationship or breakup with people in the program because I was already struggling emotionally.

However, he openly told people that we had broken up. While that may seem like a normal thing to say, I was already in a fragile state and found it extremely difficult to handle.

I eventually called my mother and told her everything that had happened because I felt unable to carry the burden alone anymore.

I also spoke to his brother and explained the situation. He told me that what had happened was wrong and that he would call me back. I never received a call.

My mother became extremely concerned about my wellbeing and eventually spoke to my ex directly.

I was also present on that call.

During the conversation, he stated that he did not know how he could be sure that the pregnancy was his and raised questions about

What I found particularly difficult was that the conversation then moved into details of our private relationship and intimate bedroom conversations. Personal matters that I believed would remain between two partners were discussed while my mother was present on the call.

For me, that was one of the most humiliating moments of the entire experience.

My mother had known him for years and was speaking to him because she was worried about my wellbeing. Instead, the conversation became focused on questioning paternity and discussing private details of our relationship.

Another thing that deeply affected me was being told that there was no future for our relationship because his family would never accept it.

During these discussions, I was also told that his family believed in honour killings. Whether that statement was intended literally or not, hearing something like that was frightening and reinforced my belief that there was no possibility of support, acceptance or resolution.

By that point, I felt completely trapped.

I was dealing with a pregnancy, an abortion, uncertainty about my health, the end of a five-year relationship and the feeling that I was carrying the consequences of everything alone.

Today, months later, my health still does not feel right.

I constantly worry that taking abortion pills without proper medical supervision may have affected me physically. I have experienced ongoing health concerns and what feels like recurrent infections. I have repeatedly wanted medical help, but I have struggled to explain the entire situation to my father because of how complicated and painful it has been.

I have repeatedly asked him to accompany me to a doctor or at least have a conversation about what happened.

He continues to keep me blocked and has refused communication.

From his perspective, the relationship ended and he chose not to remain involved.

From my perspective, I was dealing with a pregnancy, an abortion, health concerns and significant emotional distress without support from the person who was directly involved.

I am posting this because I want honest opinions.

Was it unreasonable for me to expect support, communication or assistance during and after the pregnancy and abortion?  
I understand that relationships end.

I understand that people fall out of love.

I understand that nobody can be forced to stay in a relationship they no longer want.

But what I struggle to understand is this:

Even if a relationship is over, does a person not still have some responsibility towards someone they were with for years when a pregnancy, abortion, serious health concerns and mental health struggles are involved?

Is it acceptable to completely walk away from a situation like this without communication, support, accountability or even basic empathy?

To be fair, I've come through the grieving for my grandfather a long time ago, but I wanted to share in a safe outlet and maybe someone else experienced a similar loss.

I was a little over 8 years old the first time I heard of cancer. The reason I found out was that my parents were explaining why my grandad was stuck in bed and didn't look well. Too young to understand exactly what was going on or how serious it was, I had no idea how something could be so indifferent and tear every shred of a person's being apart. Over the next 2 years I became aware of how much suffering it could cause.

As I knew my Grandad he was always an imposing man, tall and barrel chested, hardened by growing up in the depression, working hard at a local shipyard and answering the call of WWII by joining the Navy. He was a younger member of his family and had 9 sisters that adored and doted on him. From what I'm told he was quite the ladies man in his youth and I believe it. I always remember him having an air of confidence around him, like he could do anything and that he had experienced more than most would. He could be stern and strict and make you wish you could disappear with just one look, but he could also make you laugh and entertain you just as well. He made church bearable when we still went, often joking with his grandkids and sticking his dentures out of his mouth and snapping them closed and open as they stuck out, getting scolded by his grandma who took church seriously.

Part of his life experience was his undoing in the end. He had worked at a shipyard, converting ocean liners to troop transports as the war was ramping up and was exposed to large amounts of airborne asbestos. If you dont know what that is, it was used as a high heat insulator and when broken sends small fibers into the air, when you breathe them in they embed and cut the tissues in your esophagus and lungs, but what is even worse is that they cause a form of lung disease/cancer called mesothelioma.

My grandad was hit hard by the condition, at first it just seemed to make him lethargic and reduced his appetite, he lost weight and it was concerning. I was too young to know everything that was going on but I remember that he was hospitalized several times over the next year after he got his diagnosis, often times having his lungs filled with fluid and having to have them drained. All signs of his former self disappeared, he was unable to put on even the lie of a happy face for us grandkids as his daily pain level soared above anything I have known. Often times morphine was unable to even help his pain and the auto-dispenser would allow a boost as often as was safe, but a level dose is all that could have taken away his pain. As time went on I saw him wither away from a tall barrel chested man of probably close to 200 lbs, down to a gaunt frame of maybe 110 lbs, skin loose and bones showing. He had to be assisted with bathing and all bodily functions because he could barely muster the energy. For months he wasted away in unbearable pain.

One afternoon my parents packed us up in the car in a panic, I had no idea what was going on. We drove to the hospital where we met my grandma, aunts and uncles and cousins in a waiting room/lobby area. It was during the next few hours that I learned what happened. Grandad had been in so much pain and wanted to end the suffering on his own terms, not waiting for this bitch of a disease to finish him. He waited for my grandma to be in the shower, somehow summoned every ounce of strength and energy left in his body. Disconnected the IV's, walked out the front door of the house, found his snub-nosed .38 revolver that was a concealed carry in his car, walked into the side yard, put the barrel into his mouth and pulled the trigger. But after all the exertion to get to the lightest and easiest to handle gun he could access, his strength failed him and his shot did not fly true and end his life. The bullet traveled up through the roof of his mouth and up through his nose and out of the side of his nose close to his orbital socket.

The neighbors heard the shot and saw him in the yard and called the ambulance, unfortunately for him (I say this wishing he could have ended his pain right then and there) the paramedics were able to stabilize him and get him to the hospital where he stayed for a few weeks before his wound healed enough to go back to hospice care at home. Where he continued to suffer through incredible pain and nausea on a daily basis, wishing for the release that death would bring. I don't remember when he died or how everyone reacted, I think my brain blocked it out. But I was about 10 years old and couldn't process what had happened. All I knew was that he was gone, the man who showed us how to fish and crab and boat, the glue that held the extended family together was gone. I don't remember crying at his funeral/service, I think I was relieved that he wasnt in pain any longer. But over the next year I would often think of him and cry and it was always so random how it came on.

I did become more reserved after that, a quieter kid at home and at school. One of the strongest men, both in terms of body and spirit had been taken by this disease and it felt so random, and why did he have to suffer so long if nothing could be done. I determined that if somehow there was a god, he was a son of a bitch and either enjoyed the suffering of humans or he had abandoned us a long time before. The only reason I have been to a church since we stopped going as a kid, has been funerals and weddings. The sermons were just empty words and meant nothing.

My grandad was the first person close to me that died and it was a slow wasting 2 year death that was inescapable and merciless. Almost 30 years later my Dad would die from cancer that spread though most of his vital organs and lymph system, the only mercy for him and the family was that his pain only lasted for 4 months and he didn't have to linger in pain for 2 years.

I am fucking terrified that one day that will be me, wasting away, suffering and burdening my family with taking care of me and the grief of knowing that death will not come fast. I want to make sure that I dont die in a hospital bed, I want to find a way to go out on my own terms if I can or in a way that is fast, slow creeping death is the thing I fear will be my fate because all my strong male role models fell to it....cancer is a motherfucker.

I've known a guy for 2 and 1/2 years, dated once before for three months, didn't work out no big deal. But, I always had a certain feeling about him I have never had for anyone else. Just like a draw to him? If that makes sense. Even when we were not dating we kept in loose contact. It's honestly been cool to watch his life over the past few years, seeing him go from being broke af and in school with no job to now working a ton. As it stands right now, I would definitely say I love him. I've told him every other feeling I have for him except the word love and him the same toward me. Just one of those types of connections. 

We reconnected last summer (his doing) and started catching up/talking more. Saw each other here and there. Started dating in the fall. One thing I did notice pretty early on is his work takes a lot out of him. He works 12 hour overnights and on days he isn't working overnight, he works during the daytime as an instructor. Sometimes he gets maybe 4 hours of sleep, goes to work, then crashes out for 15 hours and then up and back to work. It's a high-stress job. After about four months of dating I notice some withdrawing on his end and talked to him about it. He's never been an emotion-forward guy, so I was kind of surprised when he came back and said he has been having a hard time with feeling burnt out and wanting to isolate. And I said well ok, how can I help? And he said it has nothing to do with me, it's just work, but to please work with him and be patient. As he said, "I really, really care about you." So I said ok... I could see he was trying but also struggling, and I told him it feels like you shut me out, I can see you're not doing well but the only thing I can do is watch. And he said he didn't know what was going on but he felt just so off. Anyways, I told him I am here for you and want to help you, but if you can't find a way to let me in, I can't do that. I just let him do his thing and let him know I am here for him. Anyways, I was out of town for a month and while I was gone, he told me he had been thinking about what it all means, and he knows he feels strongly enough about me to figure it out. So we agreed to talk when I returned. 

Said four hour conversation occurred, and we laid everything out on the table. Fears, insecurities, things that bother us about each other, things we love about each other, basically everything. Our thoughts on us, marriage being on the table, our feelings. It was truly a heart-to-heart. We agreed how we wanted to move forward, and I told him the only thing I really need is for you to tell me about your feelings up front. If you feel yourself withdrawing, let me know. 

That was two weeks ago. We had plans for the other night after he got off work, and he texted me and said hey, tonight won't work. I just need to say, I love seeing YOU but I legitimately don't want to see anyone right now. I am so tired and all I want to do is sleep. and I said do you mean tonight, or in general? and he called me... we were on the phone for an hour and twenty minutes. 

He said that he knows there is a problem he needs to fix, because he feels how he feels about me, but can't find it in himself to be around anyone. He told me he loves being around me, but he finds the idea of doing anything other than sitting in the dark and sleeping exhausting. It was essentially a "break up" call, but in more of a "I know something is wrong and I have to fix it" way. He said he wraps himself in work and shuts every other part of his life out and that I deserve to be met with full effort. I pushed back some and said, well from my perspective, if you feel the way you say you do, you wouldn't be doing this? And he said I stand by every thing I told you the other week and every feeling I have ever told you I have about you. He said he feels like he needs to take space to be in his bubble alone and sort out how to come out of his bubble without feeling the need to retreat. I asked the same questions probably ten times, is this it? Will we ever see each other again? Do I just stop speaking to you? Are you playing me? Is there someone else? Also, are you ok? Honestly kind of in shock. He said all he knows is right now he needs space because he can feel himself already shutting down, he thought he was in a place that he felt was turning a corner but he said he was wrong and he wants to fix it. But, he also said that it doesn't mean I can't reach out or that he won't reach out, and that he doesn't necessarily want this to be it but he knows it is not fair to make me feel like I'm in a box that he opens only when he can. 

So I said ok. I think honestly for us to ever work out, this is something you need to fix because it is a pattern I see in you. And I said this is where I need you to tell me if I'm being stupid or wasting my time. He said well I will never call you stupid, and I was like you know what I mean. I said I am going to treat this as giving you space and letting you figure your shit out, but I am not writing you or us off. Not saying I'm going to sit here and wait, but I am not closing the door because of how I see you. And if you can get yourself to a healthy spot, if it's right, I would love to know. And he said I would not be wasting my time and that he does not feel like us being together is impossible. He emphasized none of this has to do with lack of feelings or lack of anything to do with me, but truly just fixing his own behavior. 

So... what do I do? Say screw this and block him? Do what I said? I have always trusted every word he has ever told me and my honest feeling is that he is being genuine. It wasn't an easy conversation and I cried for probably half of it. I said sorry for all my feelings coming out right now, and he said you say that like I don't have a lot of those myself... it was a sucky conversation but it felt funny and soft at moments too. I'm not mad at him. It's obviously still fresh. In a way, it would be much more heart breaking but also easier if it was "I just don't have those feelings for you, I'm sorry."

For background, I’ve been seeing this woman on and off for a while now. I completely love her, but it’s been an incredibly difficult situation to deal with.

I feel like I’ve tried so hard to just be there for her, to be patient, and to love her. She’s dealing with a lot of personal things right now that no human being should ever have to go through. She has kids, and I’ve tried so hard to show her that the fact she has kids doesn’t scare me. I’m willing to work things out and try. I’ll go as slow as humanly possible until she’s comfortable with me.

The issue is that we kept sleeping together, and then she’d turn around and say she didn’t really want a relationship right now. I tried to make it very clear that I don’t want to be sleeping with somebody if it’s not leading to a relationship.

A few weeks ago, we tried talking about where we stood. She made it abundantly clear that she didn’t want a relationship and couldn’t really handle one with everything she was going through. However, she said she missed the friendship. Part of her wished we had waited longer before starting a relationship and had spent more time building a solid friendship first.

I told her I missed that too, and I asked if it was too late for us to try going back to that.

That night, I thought we were ending on good terms. Then things got confusing. We slept together, she spent the night, and then afterward she turned around and said we weren’t doing that again and that she didn’t expect to hear from me so soon.

Today, we talked on the phone for hours, just catching up. I always enjoy talking to her. It was casual, friendly conversation.

When we got off the phone, though, she told me she had some confusion and concerns about what we were trying to do. I wanted to give her space to be heard, so I offered for her to call me back so we could talk things through.

I told her, “This is the space for you to air out whatever it is you need to say. Just say it as it is, and we’ll go from there.”

She basically told me she didn’t want me to be led on. She said this was a friendship thing and that if I was still holding on to feelings, then maybe it was best that we didn’t try being friends right now until that was resolved.

I thanked her for being honest about how she felt. Then I told her that I’d been really confused by our last in-person encounter. I said that I heard her when she said she wanted to be friends, but then we’d slept together, and afterward she wanted to go right back to being friends. That confused me, and honestly, it hurt.

I wanted to make sure we were on the same page, so I said:

“What you’re trying to tell me right now is that we’re not going to be in a relationship. There’s probably no hope for that, and we should focus all of our energy solely on being friends. Am I mistaken? If I am, please let this be the time to correct that.”

And she got frustrated.

She said, “That’s all you got from the conversation? Okay.”

At that point, I started getting confused. I told her, “I’m not trying to give you an ultimatum. I’m not saying anything like that. I’m just trying to reiterate what I thought you wanted, which is for us to focus solely on being friends with no expectations.”

But she just kept getting more and more frustrated.

Eventually, I ended up crying on the phone.

She got frustrated and said, “Great, now I’m making you cry.”

At that point, I was completely confused. She kept saying things like, “I don’t know what I said. I don’t know why this reaction is happening. I don’t know why you’re upset with me. I don’t know what’s going on.”

And I kept telling her over and over again:

“I want nothing more than to be your friend. I’m not here to force a relationship on you. I just want to be your friend.”

She told me that me explaining what hurt me about our last conversation, and sharing my interpretation of what she was saying, registered to her as me telling her she was a bad person and that all she ever does is hurt me.

Then she said maybe we just shouldn’t be talking right now.

At that point, I got even more upset because I genuinely didn’t know what I’d done wrong to cause that reaction.

I kept telling her:

“I don’t want that. I want to be your friend. I want you in my life. You’re such an important person to me.”

She then started telling me that I was doing so well in life right now and that she didn’t want to ruin my day. She said maybe we should end the call so I could continue on with my day and not have her ruin anything else. She said all the frustration was given towards me but the fact that she caused me to get upset and confused.

The last thing I said was basically this:

“I recognize that you’re going through a lot, and I know you don’t mean to hurt me. I just want you to understand that if you were frustrated with yourself, I wish you would’ve said that more clearly. You’re on the phone getting really upset while I’m crying, and as the recipient of that reaction, it felt like you were upset with me. I didn’t appreciate that.”

I also told her that throughout all of our ups and downs, every time she’d told me she didn’t want a relationship, every time things got confusing, I’d tried to be patient and give her nothing but an abundance of love.

And honestly, I just don’t know what’s going on anymore.

I don’t know.

Then I hung up.

I’ve been sitting here frozen ever since, trying to figure out what happened and what I should do. She hasn’t reached back out. I don’t know if I did anything wrong. I don’t know what that entire conversation was about.

I genuinely thought she was just confused about our friendship and wanted to make sure we were both on the same page that we were only friends right now.

I don’t know how to take any of this.

I love this woman to death, but I’m not going to sit here holding my breath for years waiting to see if she ever makes up her mind about whether she wants to be with me.

She changed my life. She’s the reason I finally went to therapy, got help, and started bettering myself.

But I don’t know how to process this.

I finally got to a place where I’m functioning better mentally, and now I feel like every time I open my mouth and try to explain my point of view, something bad happens. There’s a negative reaction. It makes me feel like I’m a bad person or that I’m somehow failing to communicate properly.

So I’m wondering if anyone can give me some input.

I don’t want to be the bad person in anyone’s story. I’m just trying to figure out how I can be better and how to have a healthy friendship with this person, if that’s even possible.

Hello world, my name is J.M., but you can call me Moose. I am 15 years old, turning 16 next month, and honestly I don't even know where to begin. I've felt lonely for most of my life, but it became really bad during middle school, especially in 7th grade. The year before that, I came out as gay to my sister, but because it happened in a crowded middle school hallway, people overheard me and the news spread around the school almost instantly. My family was incredibly supportive. My mom, dad, and sister all accepted me, and I know not everyone gets that, so I am grateful for it. Unfortunately, everyone else seemed determined to make my life miserable. Rumors started spreading about me almost immediately. People said I recorded guys in the locker room with my Chromebook. People said I stared at girls' chests. People claimed I was obsessed with random straight guys. None of it was true, but once rumors start, nobody cares whether they're true or not. They just become part of who people think you are. Looking back, I genuinely think those rumors changed how people saw me for years. They gave me anxiety, destroyed my confidence, and made me feel like I was constantly being judged. Around the same time, my trichotillomania started showing up. I inherited it from my mom, and I would pull out my hair constantly. I felt disgusting. I felt ugly. I felt like a freak. I remember spending so much time hiding under hoodies and trying to disappear because I hated being seen. 7th grade was easily the worst year of my life, and while 8th grade was better, most of that year felt like I was trying to repair a reputation that had been destroyed by people who claimed they were my friends. I went to therapy. I worked on myself. I survived it. But the loneliness never really went away. I also remember coming home from school some days and completely breaking down in front of my mom. I would vent to her about everything that was happening, all the rumors, all the anxiety, all the loneliness, and I remember one day she looked at me and asked, "Where did my little boy go?" That absolutely destroyed me. I started crying immediately. She told me to come give her a hug, and I said no. Then she said, "Come on, give me a hug, it'll make you feel better." Eventually I just gave up fighting it and buried my face into her shoulder while she hugged me. That's how bad things got. I wasn't just sad, I was completely exhausted emotionally. The scary part is that I still have moments like that even today. In fact, I had one earlier before I even made this post.

Now I'm in high school, and honestly, I still feel completely alone. What hurts the most is not even the bullying anymore. It's the fact that I've never had a real relationship. I've never had my first kiss. I've never had a boyfriend. I've never had somebody look at me and think, "Yeah, that's the person I want." Before anyone says it, please don't tell me "your time will come" or "just wait." I know that's what people always say, but I am so tired of hearing it. I've already waited. I've watched other people my age get to experience all the things I've wanted for years while I sit here wondering what is wrong with me. I have ADHD. I have OCD. I have anxiety. I have high-functioning autism. I have trichotillomania. Sometimes I genuinely feel like I'm too much for people to deal with. I also have a bad habit that I'm honestly ashamed of admitting. Sometimes I end up trauma dumping on people way too early. Not because I want pity, and not because I think it's healthy, but because some stupid part of my brain thinks that if somebody knows how badly I've been hurt, they'll be less likely to leave. Like if they know how much abandonment would destroy me, maybe they'll stay. I know that's a terrible way of thinking. I know relationships don't work like that. I know it probably pushes people away more than it helps. But I can't seem to stop myself. It's like I'm so desperate to be understood that I throw my entire life story at people before they even really know me. I don't know how else to get people to understand who I am. I don't know how else to make them see the real me underneath all the anxiety, loneliness, and baggage. Sometimes it feels like if I don't tell them everything, they'll never truly know me, but if I do tell them everything, they end up leaving anyway. Maybe that's part of why this loneliness hurts so much. I don't just want somebody to like me. I want somebody to know me. The real me. Not the rumors, not the awkward kid hiding in a hoodie, not the guy people assume things about, but me. And every time someone leaves, it feels like proof that maybe being myself isn't enough. Five days ago, I told a guy I thought he was cute. He blocked me immediately. No conversation. No chance. Just blocked. That hurt more than I expected it to. And what makes it worse is seeing guys I used to like holding hands with other people while I'm still sitting here wondering why nobody ever chooses me. I don't think I'm asking for something impossible. I just want somebody who likes me. Somebody who wants to spend time with me. Somebody who doesn't make me feel annoying for caring. I love hard. Maybe too hard. I want to be able to hug my boyfriend and never want to let go. I want somebody who genuinely enjoys talking to me and wants me around. I want somebody who actually wants to call me theirs. Instead, I feel like I'm constantly searching for something that everyone else seems to stumble into naturally.

I've tried online relationships. I've had talking stages. I've done things I regret because I was desperate to feel wanted. None of it fixed the problem. The loneliness is still there. Every day. I see happy couples online. I see happy couples at school. I see videos of guys my age finding each other, falling in love, holding hands, cuddling, and doing all the normal relationship stuff, and meanwhile I'm sitting here wondering why I always seem to be left behind. My parents are extremely protective, which makes things even harder because I feel trapped between wanting independence and still being treated like a little kid. Sometimes it feels like everyone else got handed a guidebook to life that I never received. I know this post probably sounds dramatic. I know people are going to say I'm young, or that relationships aren't everything, or that I need to focus on myself first. Maybe they're right. But none of that changes how much this hurts. I don't want hookups. I don't want random online flings. I don't want fake Snapchat relationships that last two weeks. I want something real. I want somebody who genuinely loves me. Somebody who cares. Somebody who makes me feel like I'm enough. So I guess that's why I'm posting here. What am I supposed to do when I desperately want connection, but it feels like nobody wants me back? How do I stop feeling so lonely when being loved is the one thing I seem unable to find? Because honestly, I am exhausted. I am tired of feeling unwanted. I am tired of feeling left behind. I am tired of wondering what is wrong with me. And more than anything, I am tired of feeling alone.

A year ago I posted in this subreddit about how awful I felt back then: my friends didn’t care about me. I was sad as fuck. It all began when I started noticing patterns, small actions that seemed harmless when isolated. I was the butt of the joke constantly, no one else in the group was “laughed with” as much as my friends laughed with me… About me. After a while, I realised I was pretending to laugh with them just to fit in. Every joke pinched on my self esteem, grinding me down slowly. The second thing I noticed… I was the one initiating conversations or checking on them. And the third issue was that they had a much healthy relationship with each other than they had with me. I used to say yes to everything, but I lost myself trying to please them. The more they demanded from me, the more I tried to desperately please them. If they couldn’t attend each other’s needs, nothing happened. If I couldn’t do it… I would owe them. There was a constant feeling of isolation. Looking back, it was a transactional relationship where they would vent to me, use me as the butt of the joke, ask me favours. It got to a point where I couldn’t be myself anymore and I genuinely hated meeting them because I felt so much anxiety because of their comments and interactions.

One day I told them what I was going through with our relationship, and hell broke loose. Oh, I would have loved an actual fight! But… All I got was a cold, gelid treatment instead. Just silence, silence, and more silence. I went insane. I felt I was being punished for speaking out. After a while I was told “I was being too sensitive”. All the cruel jokes to me were regarded as “tough love” and personal jokes that spoke about very personal issues were regarded as “not meant to be harmful”. Two of those friends just never spoke to me anymore. The other two… They sent me a text message where they thanked me for the friendship, but they needed time away from me.

I never received an apology.

I look back and I pity myself so much. I was so fucking sad. I felt so fucking lonely, so depressed. I had to go to therapy for months after that, trying to understand what I did wrong to fuck up as much as I did to lose four people simultaneously. I obsessed about it, navigating a huge grief that made me feel so much guilt. They left a huge emptiness in me, because they took away my pride, my self esteem, my joy and their company. I circled around guilt and shame for ages, crying myself to sleep, trying to make sense of the grief.

At some point, however, I had to learn that while I didn’t do all the right things, it wasn’t my fault either. To forgive others is easier than to forgive oneself. It took months, a lot of loneliness and a lot of fear to overcome the guilt that was eating me alive. My psychologist helped me understand my friends and my own patterns. I discovered myself as a desperate people pleaser: the more I tried for everyone to be okay, the more they abused my trust. The more comfortable I tried for everyone to be, the less enjoyable were the meetings for me. I was manipulative: I didn’t meant to, but I their twisted friendship forced my low self esteem to survive one way or another.

Loneliness and the loss of those friends forced me to face my fears. I had to learn how to be a good friend again: I made MYSELF comfortable before the others, understanding that my most basic values as a human being are not to be traded for someone else’s comfort or convenience. This takes bravery if you’re socially awkward like I used to be. It takes strength and character, that I am building as I go.

I realized after a while I never lost all my friends. There was people around me that that group of friends manipulated me into thinking less of them, that knew what was going and actually held my hand while I resurfaced the grief. They had my back, and our relationship grew so much during the next months. It felt so different: I felt calmness, not once I felt laughed at. The jokes were not harmful, or personal, just normal jokes with normal friends. Normality feels so extraordinary in this grieving context. Even if I was on high alert with them, they never made me felt like a burden, or like a sensitive person. I slowly understood how manipulative people work, and when you surround yourself with decent friends things just work. No drama, no awkwardness. Just ordinary people bonding over life experiences, which is the most extraordinary thing.

The grief of losing friends at this age (or any, realistically) is so intense, so painful, specially if you’re forced to believe it’s all your fault for being sensitive. Guilt is a fucked up thing to feel when it doesn’t make sense.

Do I feel better/stronger? Yes, a bit. WIP. Am I less of a people pleaser? Yes. But I still fall on the same patterns sometimes, only to realize it way faster and redirect my impulses to make everyone happy. Am I more confident? Yes. I recently held a meet-up with strangers, it was awesome. I could feel myself again with strangers too, which is an incredible feeling. Have those old friends reached back to me? You know the answer. Of course not. They didn’t need time… They didn’t want me. They were not happy to be called out, they kicked me out of their lives. Do I miss them? I miss the idea of them that I invented to overlook their shitty actions. Have I forgiven them? I don’t think I have. I still think about the pain often. Have I forgiven myself? I think I have. It still hurts, but I think I rescued myself when I spoke out loud. I think I was holding my own hand, and I pulled out myself from that situation as good as I was able to.

If you’re going through this I just want you to know that you can survive this. It may sound exaggerated but this is one of the worst pains I’ve gone through, and the grief of losing a friend group is so real, so intense and confusing, so lonely. Sometimes I think people over 30 are supposed to have everything settled down and… Well, nope. Life can change abruptly at any age.

However, it’s never too late to start again, take your time to heal, pick up your broken pieces and discover who you can build from them.

I think the hardest part about living like this is that nobody can see how close to the edge I am. Not because I hide it particularly well, but because I’ve been carrying it for so long that it looks normal now.

The sadness is everywhere.

It sits in my chest when I wake up. It follows me through conversations. It lingers behind every laugh, every smile, every good day. It’s there when I fall asleep at night. It’s there when I have nothing to be sad about. It’s there when life is objectively good. It’s there when people tell me I should be grateful.

It’s just there. Always. Sometimes I come up for air. For a few days, maybe a few weeks if I’m lucky, the weight eases. I start to believe that maybe I’ve finally made it through. Maybe this is the time therapy worked. Maybe this medication is the right one. Maybe moving helped. Maybe the new routine helped. Maybe all the effort I’ve poured into getting better is finally paying off.

I start making plans. I start imagining a future. I start remembering what it feels like to want things. For a little while, I almost believe I might get to keep it. And then one day, without warning, it comes back. Not like a storm rolling in from the distance. More like opening my eyes underwater and realizing I never actually surfaced at all.

I was drowning the entire time. I was just close enough to the surface to mistake it for breathing. And the realization is devastating every single time. Because it means I have to start over again. I have to return to that dark place I’ve spent a lifetime trying to escape. That place where everything hurts. Where getting out of bed feels impossible. Where every task feels heavy. Where the future feels small and far away. Where existing feels like work.

And once I’m there, I stay there. For months. Months of carrying a grief I can’t explain. Months of feeling homesick for a place that doesn’t exist. Months of wishing I could crawl out of my own skin just to have a moment of peace. Months of wondering how much longer I can keep doing this. Months of watching the world continue moving around me while I feel completely frozen inside. Months of trying to remember what hope felt like before it slipped through my fingers again. Then eventually, somehow, I claw my way back toward the surface.

Not because I want to. Not because I suddenly feel hopeful. But because survival is a habit now. I come up for air. I catch my breath. And before I can even fully inhale, I’m pulled back under again. It’s been a lifetime of this.

A lifetime. A lifetime of medications. A lifetime of therapy. A lifetime of trying every coping skill, every hobby, every routine, every piece of advice people swear will help. I’ve done everything I was supposed to do. Everything. And somehow I’m still here. Still carrying this. Still waking up every day with a sadness so deep it feels ancient.

What hurts is that because I’ve learned how to function alongside it, nobody seems to understand how bad it really is. People see me go to work. They see me make jokes. They see me show up. They see me continue living.

What they don’t see is that there are days I spend every ounce of energy I have convincing myself to stay. They don’t see how exhausting it is to carry this much pain and still be expected to participate in the world as if nothing is wrong. They don’t see that sometimes I am screaming for help the only ways I know how, and nobody hears it because my voice still sounds calm.

I don’t need pity. I don’t need people to look at me and see someone broken. But sometimes I wish someone would believe me. Not fix it. Not save me. Just believe me.

Believe me when I say I’m tired. Believe me when I say I’m hurting. Believe me when I say that I am trying as hard as I possibly can. Because I don’t think people understand what it does to a person when they hurt for a lifetime.

Not days. Not months. A lifetime. What it does to keep reaching for help and still wake up feeling the same. What it does to keep hoping and keep trying and keep fighting while a small part of you slowly starts believing that maybe this is all there is.

I think people imagine giving up as some dramatic moment. A decision. A line you cross. But I don’t think that’s what it looks like.

I think giving up happens slowly. I think it starts when every new attempt to get better hurts more than the last because you have to let yourself hope again. And hope is dangerous when you’ve spent a lifetime being disappointed.

I think it happens when you become exhausted from carrying the same weight year after year and realize nobody else can feel how heavy it is. I think it happens when every version of the future looks exactly the same.  
When you stop asking yourself when things will get better and start wondering if they ever will. When you stop feeling scared of the sadness because it has become so familiar. When a small part of you starts mourning yourself while you’re still here.

Not because you want to stop trying. Not because you want to stop living. But because you are tired of hurting. Tired of hoping. Tired of fighting the same battle every day and losing it every night.

People ask me when I’m going to let myself be happy. And every time I hear it, something inside me breaks. Because they think happiness is a choice I haven’t made yet. As if I’m standing in front of a door refusing to open it. As if I haven’t spent a lifetime desperately searching for the key.

I want to be happy. God, I want to be happy. I want to know what it feels like to exist without carrying this constant ache. I want to know what it feels like to wake up and not immediately feel tired. I want to know what it feels like to look toward the future without fear. I want to know who I would have been if sadness hadn’t taken so much from me. I want to know what my life would have looked like if I hadn’t spent so much of it just trying to survive.

But wanting something and being able to have it are not the same thing. The truth is that this sadness feels woven into me now. Like fabric. Like thread stitched through every memory, every thought, every version of myself. And some days I wonder if that’s why nobody takes it seriously. Because I’ve learned how to wear it so well. Because I’ve learned how to carry it without collapsing completely. Because I’ve become fluent in suffering.

When you lose someone unexpected, excepted or even you knew it COULD happen but NEVER thought it WOULD it happen-grief becomes a constant reminder.

People talk about phone calls that change their lifes and phone calls they're never ready to have. You feel for them because you don't understand what they're dealing with and honestly you never want that understanding. But sadly, everyone is one phone call away from a different life.

This year we got that life changing phone call.

When you get that phone call nothing else matters. You take the time away from everything else if you're lucky and you run to your person. But a month, a week, a day, or an hr is never going to be enough time.  

Knowing someone is going to pass is a different type of pain. We all know our loved ones could pass at anytime but we ignore it and don't think about it til it happens. Then you realize life is to shirt and you become a poet or feel you have truly uncovered th secret to life. People change people and moments are fleeting. You sit in that for however long and once the days start to feel "normal" that fleeting feeling goes away.

You spend as much time with that person. You honor them by taking care of them. That's how you how your love. But you could've shown it better by spending more time with them before this moment. You lost seconds, days, and months and now you're losing the forever you thought you were going to have with this person. And now whatever time they have left your life is devoted to taking care of them.

You watch for little signs, everyday they eat, drink, smoke or walk you feel is another day longer. Another day longer away from the worst moment. Your body goes into survival mode because it is constantly in alert but you can't let your person know.

But no matter how hard you try to hide it, they know. They know what's coming for you as soon as they're gone.

You take secret pictures but you don't take so many because you want to be in the moments. Little silly moments happen that become bigger moments later. "Well I'm deaf in my left eye." Small moments become big moments. 

Everyone is hurting but everyone starts to forget why we're all at the house together. Just enjoying the rare moments of family time. Then something changes and we remember. We remember the reason why. We remember what's coming.

The remembering changes the air. It changes the way we breathe.

You can feel a shift in the room and you know silently everyone felt it too. You see everyone in that house is losing the same person but we're not losing the same person. That person is different things and different titles to everyone. But there's one title, one constant, one word everyone uses to describe this person, superhero. 

Not all superheros wear capes some dance to wild boy by MGK, drink out of red solo cups, curse like a ...well he wad a sailor. Not all hero's wear capes but this hero was a US navy veteran. He was our hero. He is our hero. Move over Mark Henry because this man is the world's strongest man.

You can't convince me otherwise. 

You have moments where you have scares. "You have 5 hrs left", that's impossible. There's no way. But you sit and just stare at them. You try your best to be near But after your last scream you realize you just don't have it in you to scream everytime there's a scare. So you hold it in waiting 

For the moment you'll need it. 

He pulls through and you can breathe again but also your body knows it's not over so we continue to live in survival mode. Knowing a big bang is coming and no there's not going to be anything created but more like destroyed.

You start to think maybe just maybe they were wrong. Doctors aren't all knowing maybe this time they got it wrong. Hopefully the got it wrong. Yes!!! This time they got it wrong. And you'd forgive them for getting it wrong because YES they were wrong and it's not happening. 

But you know they weren't wrong.

Unfortunately life has to keep turning so people have to leave to head home. You know they don't want to but they have too. Cars need worked on and jobs texts need answered. You hug and kiss goodbye. You're sad but can't feel any other emotion then the one you've been forced to live with for the past month.

You're blind to whats happening because of the scares and you don't completely notice the shift in the house. You stay out of the room, you don't want to make any noise, you turn your volume on your phone down, the puppies are laying around but they're not asleep.

You hear the room door bang open and you run out and you follow who flew the door open. Your brain is blank. Then you....realize.

You realize whats happening and you run back but everything is fi-....

He's gone.

That's when it happens. Your body let's out the scream it's been holding onto. Life isn't the same. The person you were before this isn't the same. Your mother, brother, bonus dad, sister, grandparents, cousins, aunt, their life's just changed.

The year went from 2025 to the year I lost you. 

You go home the next day. And reality hits you. 

Youre just so angry. Youre just so angry. That's the stage of grief that stays. You want to know why. Every tv show that has grief and lost you start quoting them. You don't understand why this happened. Nothing makes sense. 

Minutes turn to hours, hours turn to days and we'll you get the point. Every moment leads to a forever you're not ready for. When they were sick and passing you pictured all the moments they'll miss.

But here comes the moments they'll miss.

Things you would've used as excuses to text them before

"Uncle tj we got a new car."
"Yeah my job doesn't have many hrs for me"

"Uncle tj I got a new job"
"Yeah I'm going to be working both jobs"
"Lol yeah I've never worked 2 jobs before."
"Love you Uncle tj"

Are conversations you never get to have because they're not hear anymore. And you realize you didn't need excuses. 

"I love you Uncle tj"

Would've been perfect but you left your fear of annoying them get to you and now you'll never get the

"Love you too"

Ever again.

Life changed the moment they stopped breathing. You changed. The person you were before your mother sat you down, the person you were where your mother told you "couple week" that person is gone

The person you were when you were taking care of them is gone. 

The person you were a minute before they passed is gone.

The person you became AFTER they passed, that's who you are now. 

A heart broken niece to uncle you'll never hug or see again.

Grief hits you in so many ways, laughter at something that made you think about them, tears over a song on the radio, the watch scaring you at midnight because it's never gone off like that before.

Grief is the hardest and most painful reward to love.

I have this awful grief because I had someone so amazing in my life that losing them broke me.

I'll miss you forever and love you beyond that. I truly hope you always knew that. I hope you never questioned it.
