My (20F) boyfriend (19M) and I have been pretty steady and we’ve been quite happy for the last 2 years together. 

We come from a country where literally everybody is middle class. Except it’s really not the truth because some people in the same “middle class” are better off than others. Simply put, some middle class families are dual-income, have nice first hand cars & university funds for all their kids, while some could only afford a rundown beat up 2nd hand on a single breadwinner. 

In our case, my boyfriend’s the former. His parents are both teachers with a steady salary and jobs, and his elder sister also works full-time now. Despite his lack of will to get to university, (since here, we can get a diploma and work with just that credential) his parents already have the money set aside for his college education after paying for his sister and his brother. 

On the other hand, my father is a sole breadwinner to a family of 9. Having to support the rest of my family, I took on a job (and once, two jobs at a time) & bonded myself to my diploma in order to get my diploma funded & the extra allowance from the bond in order to fund my own life and support myself to have a normal teenage life. 

I never really realised growing up that I was a little less fortunate than my peers until I left secondary school. Ironic, because in my secondary school so many people lived in higher end condo apartments, while I lived in a public housing flat. My peers had the money to do extra-curriculars & go out and have nice lunches with friends, but I never did. This never used to bother me because I had different struggles on my hands. 

My boyfriend and I otherwise are pretty much the same person. We share many little details and personality traits. We have the same humour and everything has been okay for a long time. 

Recently, he had gotten his driving license in May. For context, in my country, you have to go through the driving school and pay for 2 theory tests and a lot of practical lessons. Practical lessons go up to $90+ per lesson. You have to do at least 24 of these lessons in order to be eligible to take the final test. And then the final test costs a whopping almost $400. So most people in this country pay over 1k to 2k to get the basic autocar license. 

I’ve been trying to get my license through the driving school since 2024 August. It’s now 2024 June. My boyfriend started just last year November-December. His mother paid extra for him to get the faster route to pass and get his license. 

I’ve been happy for him, of course. I’m proud that he has made it this far and has his license. It wasn’t easy either and he has his fair share of nerves. So I’ve been genuinely happy for him. 

Despite this, the last month has been rough for me. I took a month off my part-time job because I was having a recurring flu. I didn’t have any income come in and since I had to repeat a semester, I won’t be getting anymore of the school bond allowance. My parents have been struggling as well because the car they’d gotten last year secondhand has been incapacitating their finances even though it’s really dire we get the car to move around in this city. 

My boyfriend has been there for me. As usual he is a sweet man who takes care of me when I’m tired of taking care of my younger siblings as the eldest. And he’s been providing very much for me financially when we go out or when I have no money for breakfast at work and whenever I need it, despite my protests. 

However, between the license and being ridiculously broke, I’m stressed. Furthermore, my father was just in at the hospital for a checkup and found to have an artery blockage in his heart. I’m anxious and I’m worried. 

I’ve started feeling this sense of envy and bitterness that I’m struggling this much all the while my boyfriend is overseas with family on a vacation. 

I don’t blame him, of course, for any of this. I don’t blame him for the fact that he has what he does and I have what I have. Which is why I feel horrible. 

I know his mother and father and their background. I know from him how hard his mother had it when she was younger and it was a lot worse than I have it now. I know she worked very hard to get to where she is and I’m happy for their family. 

But I can’t help but be bitter when my boyfriend’s talking to me about plane annoyances when I’ve only been on a round trip flight once, on a school sponsored trip. Before then I used to yearn to go overseas and get on a plane. None of my family have even been on a plane. 

I know nothing is his fault and I know how much their family deserves this, especially his mother and grandmother. And I feel terrible for feeling bitter. 

I know my only option now is while he’s in another country having fun and enjoying a nice vacation is to just work my ass off at my job to cope. I’ve been doing that. But it just seems so bleak. It seems bleak that I’m stuck and I can’t rant about it to him. I feel like I can’t tell him how I’ve truly been feeling, because he’s been so lovely and helpful and kind to me, and if I truly told him how I felt it would sound like taking jabs at him or invalidating his family’s struggle or anything else. 

I know I can do my best to work hard to get through it and get myself out of this shitty situation after I graduate. But until then, I’m stuck. I’m stuck and my family is stuck. And above all I bonded three years of myself to a career I can’t tolerate and can’t see myself doing long term. I’m pretty miserable and for now, I can’t do much but to just keep my emotions regulated & work. Which is why I’m ranting on here. 

Thank you to anyone who is reading this. It’s silly and honestly I feel like I’m whining and being a bit of a brat. But thank you for your time.

Hey guys - so here it goes. I am 35 years old and just battled breast cancer treatment from August 2025 to April 2026. I went through double mastectomy, chemotherapy, and 16 rounds of radiation. I met - let's call him Mark - who is 51M, and we met online between my diagnosis and treatment. Mark was super kind, very articulate and although he was originally not my type, I grew to develop loving feelings for him and attachment.

At this time, like with many cancer survivors, I was ghosted by my family and my friends were over a thousand miles away. My sister was also long distant and she too sadly got diagnosed with breast cancer.

I was alone and I was in a vulnerable position. I live in a dilapidated studio which is all I could afford given my short term disability from a non-profit job. Mark felt deeply bad and wanted to open his house to have me stay there for a few months while I was undergoing treatment so he could be there for me. He took me to appts. I took and received his help. Overtime, I fell in love with him.

What I also noticed was that he was very much close friends with Betsy (not real name) his ex wife of 15 years. He said their marriage ended due to a dead bedroom and that he had a failing liver from an auto immune disease and had a year of darkness that he does not discuss further. He said he saw a future in me yet he made it very clear he would always be friends with Betsy and be very close to her.

At first, I saw that as a green flag. Because I am friends with my ex, Jim, of over 15 years and I think friendships can come from ex partners. But eventually, I noticed he was deeply intertwined in her family affairs and would talk about Betsy doing this and Betsy doing that. He flew to her home state to fix her lawn mower and even stayed at her ex- mother in law's house while sending me pics of him with his ex wife's dog. He had her fertility letters that he mentioned were signed over to her during their divorce coming to his mail which, gotta admit, hit my insecurity as I was battling chemo and loss of fertility and I couldn't afford to freeze my eggs. Apparently the fertility letters were their shared embryos as he mentioned they tried to conceive but she miscarried.
Whenever she called- whether it was about her personal life drama or when he reached out for advice for applying for a job, she was his immediate person. I also noticed that his family even made comments comparing me to her. It was getting deeply uncomfortable.

He also taped nicotine and did not disclose this on his dating profile, arguing that there is no evidence based on chatgpt that I would get breast cancer recurrence. He argued with me during my first night of chemo until 5am. As much as he cared for me and did husband like behaviors, he would also be ambiguous about our future saying " let things unfold."

. Anytime I sought reassurance about us, he would scoff, dismiss, and would avoid " relationshipy talks." He would defend, deflect, argue and go full on attorney mode on me. He would raise his voice and storm away because he was irritated by my neediness.

He then broke up with me in january of this year in the middle of my third round of chemo because we started having arguments. He wanted Betsy to stay at his house after she said she was willing to buy season holder tickets for him as he wanted extra cash. He then tells me that she and him made plans for the weekend without even my input and that I would meet his family along with her and then he and her would go to the football game together because " i should stay home as my immune system is suppressed." I had no choice but to agree with it as my housing and treatment was dependent to my relationship status. But I was resenting it and eventually I asked him if he disclosed my breast cancer diagnosis in spite of me telling him from the beginning and he told her he did share I had cancer.

Thats when I told him how I felt betrayed from that and he screamed " get the fuck out you fucking psycho!" I left.

--- in March, he asks me to rekindle. I did give him, regrettably, another chance because he mentioned how he was in individual therapy and working on himself. I told him I am traditional minded and I want a serious level of commitment after all that we have been through and suggested couples therapy which he said he was open to, in order to address our communication differences. I told him I would manage to work on my trust issues and with issues regarding him and Betsy as he said he would limit interactions with her now that he found out she was marrying someone else he did not agree with.

Then a few weeks later, it happened again. His dog sadly passed and I was there to support him. He and Betsy shared their dogs and I suggested he call Betsy as their dog was in his final breath. He then called her " Baby" several times which cut me to the core. I let it go because I understood maybe it was the context yet I felt like it was a Freudian slip.

He started to miss out on therapy sessions and stopped going, saying he did not need it, yet showed the similar irritation and raising of his voice. I felt like I had to walk on eggshells. He did limit interactions with Betsy and did try to inform me of every interaction he had with her, which I did not even ask for, but that he was willing to provide.

Yet the straw that broke our relationship again was when he answered her call at an odd hour on a sunday. He was super anxious about her feelings about his ex mother in law. I told him it was infiltrating our time and she called him for a quick Google search that she could have asked her fiance.

That led to us arguing as Mark became increasingly defensive and defended her over me. I finally shared this with my therapist and he advised I point blank ask for proof of divorce papers because I felt like they were behaving like they were still married.

Of course, I did, and then he threw the trust argument, sent me screenshot and said " go f@#$% yourself."

Hi, I hope this format is okay for this subreddit as I'm not really sure how else to go about this. This is simply to get 20+ years of emotions out and try to begin the healing process. I'll apologize now for the length that this post may reach - I'm not sure if anyone will bother to read this through to the end, and thats okay if you dont! This is simply for me to have an outlet to get this out. I'll simply go by Koop. I'm 35 years old as of a couple months ago, but I never intended to make it into adulthood. To get there, I feel I need to go back to when everything started going downhill for me. So lets rewind to 2002 when my parents split.   
I lived a really good life up until that point. Loving parents, loving grandmother, I couldnt have asked for anything better. Then 2002 came, my parents split, and I was suddenly uprooted by my mother and taken to another state because she'd met a man she thought could change her life. That's around the time everything changed. He was nice enough at first - and she was still the mother I thought was there to protect me from everything and everyone. I was 11 at that time.
2 weeks after being moved to a new state was the first time she punched me in the face. A few weeks later was the first time he locked me out of the house in 100+ degree weather without food or water until i push mowed the 5 acre lawn. I was told it was good for me, it was "character building".   
These kinds of things happened pretty regularly for a few months. Then she found out she was going to have another child, only this one wasnt going to survive birth (she knew this and chose to give birth anyways, which i wont fault her for). 
Fast forward to 2003 and my grandmother passing from lung cancer. I knew it was coming because we would visit occasionally and I watched her health decline rapidly. The woman who loved me unconditionally and that I still struggle with her death to this day, 23 years later. I went into a depressive state after she died which was only further worsened by the passing of my sibling after he was stillborn and my developing type 1 diabetes. Thats when my mother started..changing. I always believed it was because she couldnt handle the death of her child, but recently I think its just that she had been in over her head for a long time.
After that, her marriage ended rather quickly and she went through a stage of bringing multiple flings around. Some not so bad, some not so great. That was the norm for.. a while. Until she met a new romance that she, again, thought could change her life for the better. He was..tolerable at best. IIRC, his favorite thing to say was "until I see a mf walk on water, the only God in this house is me." I believe I was 14 or 15 at the point we moved in with him. I was still pretty depressed in general at this point, and then he decided that he didn't appreciate me eating food when they weren't home, so he placed padlocks on all the cabinets that contained food, drilled holes into the tops of the fridge and placed a padlock there that kept the fridge and freezer from opening, and placed a padlock on the deep freeze. Which made it so he and my mother could control when I ate (I was allowed to eat dinner and breakfast if they felt like getting up to make breakfast). My character building was mowing the yard and chopping firewood, which only eating once or twice a day, and small portions, usually meant I didnt have the strength to get very far in either thing, which I was punished for (hit with belts, punched). 
So that's when I decided to end everything because I felt that was my best option. The crazy part here.. is I succeeded. I was dead for minutes on that emergency room table until the doctor on duty successfully got me back. I spent months in a medically induced coma. My mother had made sure that she made it so that no friends were allowed in to see me during that time, and she herself didnt come either. I was finally released a few weeks after coming out of the coma, and the first thing she did was load me into the truck and drive me to a mental institution. She checked me in and told them I'd tried to kill myself. They got me through the initial process (checked all my bags, took my shoe laces and laces out of my hoodies and shorts) and then she left. I was only in there for less than 24 hours before they called her to come get me because they couldnt administer my insulin due to the sliding scale that I was on. So after checking me out, her next idea was to take me across state lines to her friends house and leave me there in the middle of the night, while she herself went back to be with the same man. (I found out later that hed told her it was me or him, so she made her decision). Within 12 hours, my dad (the man she was married to originally - but was not my actual father) drove to that friends house, picked me up, brought me back to his new home and began the paperwork to adopt me - with the caveat being that he had to have her drive down and admit, to a judge, that shed abandoned me. Which she did - after he agreed that hed never ask her for a dime in child support.
I spent the rest of my teenage years and into my early adult years feeling..nothing. I slept around because honestly I just wanted someone to love me. I wanted to feel some form of love because it had been years since I'd felt like anyone even so much as cared about me. I know my dad did, but I didnt think he understood (and I dont think he understands even to this day) the life I had to live with her and her significant others. I've tried giving my mother multiple chances in life, up until about 2 months ago. She's never been able to admit any wrongdoing, but about a year ago she told me she forgave me for everything I'd ever caused her to do. Wonderful woman, right? I need to backtrack to 2013 for a moment, as thats when my daughter was born. Her mother and I didnt work out, it was mutual destruction on both of our parts. In 2014 though.. in 2014 I met the woman of my dreams. The one who saw me and didnt CARE that I was broken goods. Who wanted to fix me because I was fixing her as well. She loved my daughter immediately, and I loved her daughter as well. We moved in together within months of meeting and we havent looked back since. I married her in 2023 and even to this day we still build each other up. About 2 months ago, I received one final text from my mother and all it read was "you should have killed yourself when you had the chance all those years ago". I didnt respond to that message, I simply deleted it and blocked her number then reflected on why I ever thought that maybe I really was the problem, maybe I did deserve the life I was given. All she ever did was tore me down and tried to make me less than I was. I think this is where I'll be ending this post..I think ive gotten most, if not all, of everything off my chest and I can try to begin healing now. If you made it through this post that I, personally, consider far too long, thank you. Thank you for taking the time out of your day. Much love <3

Hi, I hope this format is okay for this subreddit as I'm not really sure how else to go about this. This is simply to get 20+ years of emotions out and try to begin the healing process. I'll apologize now for the length that this post may reach - I'm not sure if anyone will bother to read this through to the end, and thats okay if you dont! This is simply for me to have an outlet to get this out. I'll simply go by Koop. I'm 35 years old as of a couple months ago, but I never intended to make it into adulthood. To get there, I feel I need to go back to when everything started going downhill for me. So lets rewind to 2002 when my parents split.

I lived a really good life up until that point. Loving parents, loving grandmother, I couldnt have asked for anything better. Then 2002 came, my parents split, and I was suddenly uprooted by my mother and taken to another state because she'd met a man she thought could change her life. That's around the time everything changed. He was nice enough at first - and she was still the mother I thought was there to protect me from everything and everyone. I was 11 at that time.

2 weeks after being moved to a new state was the first time she punched me in the face. A few weeks later was the first time he locked me out of the house in 100+ degree weather without food or water until i push mowed the 5 acre lawn. I was told it was good for me, it was "character building".

These kinds of things happened pretty regularly for a few months. Then she found out she was going to have another child, only this one wasnt going to survive birth (she knew this and chose to give birth anyways, which i wont fault her for).

Fast forward to 2003 and my grandmother passing from lung cancer. I knew it was coming because we would visit occasionally and I watched her health decline rapidly. The woman who loved me unconditionally and that I still struggle with her death to this day, 23 years later. I went into a depressive state after she died which was only further worsened by the passing of my sibling after he was stillborn and my developing type 1 diabetes. Thats when my mother started..changing. I always believed it was because she couldnt handle the death of her child, but recently I think its just that she had been in over her head for a long time.

After that, her marriage ended rather quickly and she went through a stage of bringing multiple flings around. Some not so bad, some not so great. That was the norm for.. a while. Until she met a new romance that she, again, thought could change her life for the better. He was..tolerable at best. IIRC, his favorite thing to say was "until I see a mf walk on water, the only God in this house is me." I believe I was 14 or 15 at the point we moved in with him. I was still pretty depressed in general at this point, and then he decided that he didn't appreciate me eating food when they weren't home, so he placed padlocks on all the cabinets that contained food, drilled holes into the tops of the fridge and placed a padlock there that kept the fridge and freezer from opening, and placed a padlock on the deep freeze. Which made it so he and my mother could control when I ate (I was allowed to eat dinner and breakfast if they felt like getting up to make breakfast). My character building was mowing the yard and chopping firewood, which only eating once or twice a day, and small portions, usually meant I didnt have the strength to get very far in either thing, which I was punished for (hit with belts, punched).

So that's when I decided to end everything because I felt that was my best option. The crazy part here.. is I succeeded. I was dead for minutes on that emergency room table until the doctor on duty successfully got me back. I spent months in a medically induced coma. My mother had made sure that she made it so that no friends were allowed in to see me during that time, and she herself didnt come either. I was finally released a few weeks after coming out of the coma, and the first thing she did was load me into the truck and drive me to a mental institution. She checked me in and told them I'd tried to kill myself. They got me through the initial process (checked all my bags, took my shoe laces and laces out of my hoodies and shorts) and then she left. I was only in there for less than 24 hours before they called her to come get me because they couldnt administer my insulin due to the sliding scale that I was on. So after checking me out, her next idea was to take me across state lines to her friends house and leave me there in the middle of the night, while she herself went back to be with the same man. (I found out later that hed told her it was me or him, so she made her decision). Within 12 hours, my dad (the man she was married to originally - but was not my actual father) drove to that friends house, picked me up, brought me back to his new home and began the paperwork to adopt me - with the caveat being that he had to have her drive down and admit, to a judge, that shed abandoned me. Which she did - after he agreed that hed never ask her for a dime in child support.

I spent the rest of my teenage years and into my early adult years feeling..nothing. I slept around because honestly I just wanted someone to love me. I wanted to feel some form of love because it had been years since I'd felt like anyone even so much as cared about me. I know my dad did, but I didnt think he understood (and I dont think he understands even to this day) the life I had to live with her and her significant others. I've tried giving my mother multiple chances in life, up until about 2 months ago. She's never been able to admit any wrongdoing, but about a year ago she told me she forgave me for everything I'd ever caused her to do. Wonderful woman, right? I need to backtrack to 2013 for a moment, as thats when my daughter was born. Her mother and I didnt work out, it was mutual destruction on both of our parts. In 2014 though.. in 2014 I met the woman of my dreams. The one who saw me and didnt CARE that I was broken goods. Who wanted to fix me because I was fixing her as well. She loved my daughter immediately, and I loved her daughter as well. We moved in together within months of meeting and we havent looked back since. I married her in 2023 and even to this day we still build each other up. About 2 months ago, I received one final text from my mother and all it read was "you should have killed yourself when you had the chance all those years ago". I didnt respond to that message, I simply deleted it and blocked her number then reflected on why I ever thought that maybe I really was the problem, maybe I did deserve the life I was given. All she ever did was tore me down and tried to make me less than I was. I think this is where I'll be ending this post..I think ive gotten most, if not all, of everything off my chest and I can try to begin healing now. If you made it through this post that I, personally, consider far too long, thank you. Thank you for taking the time out of your day. Much love <3

I (29 F) have been with my boyfriend (28 M) for 5 years. And been living together for a couple of years.

Before I say anything else, I want to be fair.

He is not cruel. He is not a bad man. He cares about me, he accepts me for who I am, he never gets physical, and I know he loves me (?). I love him.

But lately I’ve been sitting with a very uncomfortable feeling and I genuinely do not know whether I’m being unreasonable, or whether I’ve spent years slowly abandoning parts of myself without realizing it.

The issue is not one specific fight. The more I think about it, the more I realize this extends far beyond just romance or little disagreements.

Early in our relationship, because of things I’ve experienced in the past and because I’ve dealt with harassment in public more times than I can count, we created a code word together. It was supposed to be my panic button if we were somewhere and I suddenly felt unsafe around someone. I’d say the word, and the agreement was simple: we leave.

In the roughly ten times I’ve used it over the years, I can only remember him actually listening maybe twice.

The other times, his response was usually some variation of: “There’s nothing.”

And every time I’d think… well, sure. For you there’s nothing. But you are not the one feeling unsafe. My heart is racing over here.

Another example. Whenever we take trains or public transport, I tend to keep walking through the carriages until I find a place where I feel comfortable sitting. I pay attention to who is around me, I notice groups of men or women. I notice people behaving strangely. I notice things because unfortunately I’ve learned in the past that I have to.

And sometimes while I’m doing this, he gets annoyed and says: “Why can’t we just sit?”

And I always find myself thinking: after five years together, after everything I’ve explained to you about what I’ve experienced, how do you still not understand why I do this?

It’s exhausting that I constantly have to justify basic things I do to feel safe.

Even small moments feel like this. Sometimes I’ll quietly whisper something to him in public because I obviously do not want other people hearing what I’m saying.

And instead of understanding that I’m whispering for a reason, he’ll loudly respond: “Huh? What?”

And then insist I repeat myself right there, out loud, even when I clearly do not want to. I don’t know if this man can’t read a social cue or what? But he seems like a smart guy to me, having a master degree and all.

I’ve realized that over the years, whenever I express wanting something, whether romantic, spontaneous, or simply different, his immediate reaction is almost always some version of no.

A recent example:

This evening, we were watching a romance movie together (I already felt like a I was burdening him because he never wants to watch romance movies with me despite me going through re-runs of the hobbit plenty of times for him, and no i do not hate the hobbit but i am a ‘watch a movie only once’ kind of girl - unless I forget how the story went).

Anyways, there was a scene where the guy gently took off his jacket and placed it over the girl’s shoulders. Just a simple gesture but it was so freakin’ cute.

So I looked over at him. And he immediately said: “You never want my jacket.”

I laughed and said: “Well… because you wear hoodies. They don’t fit me. She’s getting a jacket.” Mind you, my boyfriend is slimmer than I am. I won’t say I’m massive, but definitely NOT his size. And jackets tend to be oversized, i could do a jacket. Not a hoodie. His hoodie would hug my frame and show all my curves, not what a hoodie was meant to be like.

And immediately he responded: “Don’t compare me to other men.”

And I thought… I wasn’t comparing you. I was simply watching a moment that made me think: I wish I experienced more thoughtful romantic gestures. But of course I got emotional and turned off the movie and went to bed, because now the moment was just ruined. AND THIS MAN, not long after, he went to bed acting like nothing had happened despite claiming he hates when someone does that.

This has been a recurring issue because throughout our relationship I’ve often shown him little gestures I find sweet or romantic.

And his response is usually: “I’m not like that. Don’t try to change me.”

Another example. One night I woke up with an extremely painful cramp in the middle of the night. I woke him up because I was in pain.

Instead of helping me or even asking if I was okay… he got angry at me for talking about something like that while he can barely process it as he’s half asleep. Fair enough.

But well well well. I now know I’m fked if we ever get robbed in the middle of the night.

I admit I became emotional. This was probably one of our worst fights. I think something about that reaction triggered me because in that moment I just wanted comfort like a hug. I knew the cramp would go away, but damn… did he have to react like that?

And when I get overwhelmed, I tend to shut down temporarily because I need space to regulate myself.

Sometimes that takes a few hours. I communicated that I needed space. Instead, he insisted we talk about it immediately.

Which turned me being hurt into a full argument because suddenly I was forced to defend my feelings while still emotionally sensitive. I don’t do well in such situations.

I just couldn’t believe that the biggest argument in years of our relationship was because of THIS?

Another example.

I saw a photo of a male K-pop idol whose hairstyle I thought looked really nice.

Before people jump to conclusions, I was not thirsting over celebrities. But I admit, they are very good looking people and just look so stylish. My boyfriend has had essentially the exact same hairstyle for as long as I know him. And looking at his pictures, probably the last 15 years.

I thought maybe trying something different could be fun. So I showed him the picture and said I liked the hairstyle.

His immediate response: “I’m not a K-pop idol.” And I just thought… okay? It was literally a simple curtain cut hairstyle.

It wasn’t some impossible fantasy haircut that would look funny on a normal guy. I wasn’t asking him to become another person.

But this happens constantly.

I love karaoke. “No. I don’t sing.” Until this day, we’ve never done karaoke. I sing like a whale, but i still like the karaoke atmosphere.

I love spontaneous nights ordering pizza, eating junk food, watching movies, staying up talking. I used to do it with my roommate and LOVED the bond that grew between us “No. I don’t do that.”

I suggest a city trip. “We did one recently.” (Recently = two months ago.)

And I’m starting to realize this isn’t about isolated situations. It’s that every attempt I make to bring spontaneity, romance, fun, or shared experiences into our relationship immediately gets shut down.

And what scares me most is what I’ve noticed about myself. Before this relationship, I was extremely social.

I constantly saw friends. I traveled. I did spontaneous things. I regularly called friends who live overseas. I was energetic and expressive.

Now I barely see my friends twice a month. I feel quieter. Less spontaneous. Like parts of my personality have slowly been dimmed over the years. And I want to be very clear. He has never told me not to see friends or stop doing things.

This is not that.

It feels like over time I have adapted to living around someone whose default response to so many things I enjoy is rejection or resistance.

And I love this man deeply. I truly do. Which is why I feel guilty even writing this. But I can’t stop thinking: Is it normal to feel like you’re losing parts of yourself in a relationship?

Am I asking too much by wanting someone who ‘occasionally’ says yes to the things that bring me joy?

Or have I spent 5 years convincing myself that constantly feeling dismissed is somehow normal?

What do you think?

Me and my Fiancee's (let's call him Balls- :P) have known each other since 2016. Friends first, casual dating and some back and forth, then seriously together since 2023.

Me and Balls got engaged on 7th August 2025. Wedding was set for 12th December 2026.

Balls used to be avoidant, had ADHD, and the first year or two of our relationship was rocky because of it. We went to therapy together and worked through it. Therapy worked for the both of us... I watched him go from avoidant to genuinely secure. He proposed to me just 2 days before our Roka (Formal engagement in Indian culture). Balls took me on a date to a place where we had our first actual date, he booked that exact same seat where we sat many years ago and proposed to me on that exact table. I was genuinely shaking and at first I have him back the ring because I was so fucking nervous. It was one of the best moments of my life. He's someone who didn't even believe in marriage as an institution, and he told everyone- my mom, our friends, me, that I was the only person he'd ever marry.

Our relationship was genuinely amazing... people looked at us and envyed what we had. I had my friends, my flatmates, even my cousins tell me that they looked at us, and it made them believe in love again...

Then as the wedding dates came close, his parents started raising issues about wedding expenses. Their behaviour quietly but noticably shifted. They had a problem with what I would wear on MY wedding to why were so involved in the planning... His parents turned disrespectful toward my family... In one of the conversation where our parents were discussing expenses one of his relatives told my father that bearing all the expenses is the responsibility of the girl's parents. Even asked my father how he wasn't aware of this "tradition" didn't my father ever get married, not not know this?" I had a respectful but direct conversation with his parents calling out the disrespect. His mother's ego got bruised. His parents called off the wedding.

He told me afterward that I wasn't wrong to speak up and that my parents had genuinely been disrespected. But he also said I shouldn't have spoken back to his mom at all, even respectfully, because in his family kids just don't do that.

Weeks of painful back and forth followed, him swinging between his own distress and blaming me for speaking up. I set a boundary: I'd only talk in person about our future, not rehash the past or be told decisions that had already been made without me. I told him I loved him and wasn't leaving, but I wasn't going to keep standing next to someone who didn't see me as an equal in this.

My mom eventually spoke to him directly and gave him a window to decide if he could commit to a future with me.

The next day he called me. We talked for over an hour. It turned into an argument... He had decided to end it. Years of friendship and our shared future... He had decided to end it without even seeing me in person. So... He ended it, on the phone, saying he didn't think this could ever be solved even with conversations, and that he couldn't look at me the same way anymore because I'd "ruined our future." By speaking up. He told me he didn't want to see me in person because he was scared he'd lose himself to anger and say or do something irreparable.

I sent him a long goodbye message on WhatsApp. I didn't want that argument to be our last conversation.

The strange part is I'm not angry at him. I saw him cry for the first time in the ten years I've known him., after a fight with his father. The only other time he's ever cried, by his own account, was when he failed a major competative exam, four years ago. I understood the pressure he was under from his family. I just didn't want our last real conversation to be a fight, so I made sure my last words to him were gratitude, not bitterness.

Now I'm just grieving. Some moments I hope he comes back. Some moments I don't want him to. I miss him and I want to be over him, sometimes in the same hour. I don't think I'm looking for him to come back so much as I needed to say thank you and goodbye properly, which I think I did. I felt safe when I was in that relationship even when he wasn't around, I felt safe that he existed. Now I am going places alone.. third wheeling my friends. Crying myself to sleep. I felt like I've been left on an abandoned road by the guy who was supposed to protect me for the rest of my life. The thought of being with someone else or going on a date with another man makes me want to vomit. I am not angry at him. I just feel abandoned by my the one person who was supposed to protect me.

I spoke to two of our common friends, both told me he always knew that wedding expenses and dowry was something that he knew would become a problem. But he never spoke to me about it. I just feel like someone who will be tossed around for IFK how long because she truly trusted a guy to show up as a man.

His parents think I spoke up against them, and I will ruin their family. They are okay with their son never marrying.. but they can't even look at me because I disrespected them.

He was on that call when I spoke to them. He wasn't on mute, if I was disrespectful to his parents he could have stopped me. But he stood there helpless. Like he was paralysed. Yes he did send me some WhatsApp messages while I was talking to his parents. But I use Android and not Iphone. So I did not see those messages while speaking to them. His mother was especially disrespectful to me. I just answered her back. Not disrespectfully, but I did answer her back. If he thought I was being disrespectful he could've stopped me on that call. But he didn't. Now he blames me for ruining "our future". He initially agreed that I wasn't disrespectful but not anymore. Now he says he can't even talk to me about our future because he thinks I am not "qualified enough" to take descisions because standing up for disrespect was so important to me that I didn't even care about what we had.

Everyone I speak to says I dogged a bullet. Even he says I deserve better...

I just cry myself to sleep almost every night since then, because looking at Balls standing there helpless made me see him differently. I thought he was the man of my dreams. And there he was, man of my dreams, not saying anything, not doing anything. Later flipping the script on me.

Every day I feel that it's impossible to get over this. I am not angry at him but I still feel betrayed. I don't know how I will ever trust anyone else.

I guess I'm not really asking for advice. I just needed to put this somewhere outside my own head.

That bastard looked at you like you hung the moon, and I was just some guy who fed him every day. Criminal.

But I think about you. And I think about the fact that you wanted to live a little, because of me.

So, I owe you the same.

And if, somewhere down the line, I happen to get hit by a truck or lightning or catch a stray bullet as an innocent bystander in the middle of some wild police chase – I'll welcome that with open arms. Because then I'd finally get to be with you again.

So, if anybody ever tells me I was crazy to go on my first date on my birthday, I'll smile and say, "Yes. I was crazy enough to give myself the best birthday gift I ever got."

And she’s the love of my life. 

I love you, my Passenger Princess. I hope you finally found the peace you always deserved.

Trigger warning: death of a parent 

Hopefully if you've made it this far, you understand that I'm going to talk about my dad, who died about 2.5 hours ago. 

My dad and I had a very up and down relationship, but over the last 6+ years, he was one of my best friends and was part of my inner support system. 

Due to sibling issues that I was unable to overcome (I won't discuss what happened, but it's something that I may post about later), I wasn't with him when he passed away. I will say that I was invited back by the staff, even after I made some large mistakes including losing my temper and swearing in my dad's room. That was the ONLY thing they did correctly the entire time. 

My dad, about four weeks before his death, called me and told me he didn't want to be a vegetable. He said that if he was going to be impaired in any way mentally, that he would want a DNR. 

Fast forward to Tuesday afternoon, around 12:42 PM, my life changed forever. I was driving around, running errands with my partner. We were actually done with errands and were planning on heading home to take a nap. My phone rang, and it was the hospital calling. 

They said my dad had come in the previous day for an elective procedure in his leg. They told me that the procedure was successful, and that he was stable until around 10 pm. At around 10 pm, he had a heart attack that required shocking his heart at least 3 times and CPR twice. 

We were only a block or two away from home when they finally said he was still alive, but that no one was there to make decisions for him and they asked me to come to the hospital. I've been unemployed for two years so we didn't have the money to make the drive, let alone being able to afford a place to stay. 

My partner, my wife, and I didn't hesitate. We left within the hour, and we got to the hospital around 5:30 pm. 

As soon as we arrived, a doctor that had called us on the drive to the hospital specifically made it a point of tracking me down and telling me that Dad had told him before he was sedated that he wanted a DNR if he lost any mental acuity. 

After that doctor finished talking to me, another group of doctors came to me in the waiting room. These doctors presented themselves as the ones in charge. They told me they needed me to make a decision on his care right then. I was already in shock from the phone call and then numbly driving several hours. I hadn't peed yet. That's how immediately I got jumped and pressured into making a decision. 

The third time they asked me to decide what to do, I broke down. I started sobbing and asked if I could see him first. They said yes, but they warned me about the tubes, wires, and machines keeping him alive. I had seen him like that before so I was confident in my ability to go see him. 

I walked down the hall alone. I asked my wife and partner to stay back so I could see him on my own. As I entered the room and turned to look towards the bed, I wasn't prepared to see what I saw. It was his body, but as I looked at him and as I held his hand, I knew then that he was already gone. He was gone. This was just an empty vessel. A shell that was now empty. Sure, he was on a massive amount of medication and at least three different machines were keeping his heart beating and blood flowing. They were keeping his lungs pulling in and out oxygen so he could breathe, but I was under no illusions. This wasn't my dad. It was just his body. 

I don't believe in God. I am an Atheist, after spending my first 36 years of life being a member of a very prominent religion, I no longer believe in an afterlife. I'm still not quite sure what I believe, but no matter what I believe or don't believe, that was a body without a soul. Whatever it is that's inside us, keeping us with our bodies, that was gone and dad was gone, while his body lay before me.

I did all the right things, as far as communication with my siblings, with his mom, with his brother and sister. Keep in mind, of all my siblings, I was the closest in terms of distance, and I also believe that I was closest to him in terms of a relationship. 

Most of my siblings haven't spoken to or had any kind of relationship with our dad in at least six years. 

Two of my siblings talk to him on the phone. The rest have no contact with him. Me? I talked to him weekly. We talked about everything from life, death, taxes, politics (we never saw eye to eye so we usually needed to avoid those conversations lol), about my family, he asked about my three kids, he asked about my wife, my partner, and how things were with me. 

He recently invited me to go to an MLB game that my youngest sister was going to be part of a group that was singing the National Anthem. I was really excited for that as I haven't been to a game in a few years. 

Anyhow, I didn't get a chance to say goodbye before everything got messed up. And I don't regret that I tried with everything I could to honor his request of having a DNR. Unfortunately, all the siblings that hadn't been around for most of the last six years showed up, and they went behind my back and forced the hospital to remove the DNR that he asked for. 

This is the part of the story where I made some mistakes. I have owned my mistakes to those that matter to me. That's why I don't plan on telling this part of the story. So fast forward to last night.

The hospital has gathered all my siblings, including those that were unable to be there in-person. I got a call from my older sister, and she explained that they were going to talk to us all about some things. 

They then read a paragraph about how they determine who has control over decisions for our dad. This was at 8:32 pm on Wednesday. Based on their own policy, they should have done the exact same thing but we should have had a conference call with all the siblings who cared to have a voice in his decisions on Tuesday at 5:30 pm when I arrived. I wasn't given an option to call everyone. I was told to make a decision, and that if I knew what dad wanted, that I should tell them what that decision was. 

After seeing my dad, I knew he wouldn't want to be shocked over and over again. He has suffered from terrible health issues, including mental health issues. He was miserable his last couple years alive. He told me on more than one occasion that he didn't want to live like that. 

He passed today at 2:28 PM. I never got a chance to say goodbye to him before I left and drove back home. I know that it was the right decision for me, but it hurts so much that I no longer have a dad and I no longer have siblings either. 

Maybe I'll change my mind. Maybe I won't. Either way, I know he knows I did all I could for him. And I know he knows how much I love him. Even though I didn't say goodbye to him.

As a kid I was so painfully shy, but other adults would laugh it off, reassuring my parents it was just a phase. "My kids were like that, now they won't shut up! You'll see." I'm 30 and thing have only gotten worse. 

While I do believe my parents genuinely love me, I always had the impression they care more about what others thought than whatever I was feeling. When I accidentally revealed to my mom I was if not trans, at the very least gay by asking what I thought was an innocent question, she reacted angrily and told me never to repeat that again, specially not in front of my dad. I was a perfectly behaved child, I got good grades and went on to have the best grades in the entire school. Yet for my dad it was never good enough. He always treated me like I was a deviant, to this day he will assume the absolute worse for me in any given situation.

I managed to make friends in middle school, and even had a best friend for 6 years. We were inseparable and did everything together. There were signs he was an asshole, but I chose to ignore it. After all, my own dad was such an asshole to me, it seemed normal. We spent the entire school day together, then talked for hours on the phone, and on weekends we were always at each other's houses. Our parents became close and got along really well. But my parents never really liked him. My dad resented that he was clearly the domineering one, he raised me to be a doormat and expected me to be a leader somehow. My mom on the other hand was alwas intriguing, trying to put us against each other. One time my friend even asked me why my parents didn't liked him.

As middle school was almost over, we arranged to go to the same high school, so we could continue to be together. I was so excited to move to a big, cooler school with my best friend. I was on the top of the world. In our 8th grade graduation, a teacher said I laughed at every joke, even if it was bad. I had somehow grown into a shy, but talkative class clown of sorts. I remember my first few tastes of "freedom", going into a weekend trip with the rest of my class with some of our teachers, away from our parents. And after our graduation, we went just us kids to eat pizza at a nearby restaurant. My mom "jokingly" insisted she wanted to come, but my dad forbade her. It was the first time I went to a restaurant without my parents and paid for my meal. I was 14, I never did that again. 

High school was pure hell. My best friend became distant, and the memory of me literally following him as he briskly tried to get away from me during lunch breaks still hurts. I tried to pretend everything was fine, we still talked on the phone after school, but now he just asked about homework. We went out one final time, my dad took us to the movies to watch Shutter Island. We watched the movie, walked a bit on the mall, and at night had some fast food. I grew up with an emotionally abusive mom. I have vivid memories of her screaming at me, calling me r\\d and boyish, making fun of my appearance, and telling me she wished I was never born. She'd often say that I'd never have friends, graduate from college, or get a job. When I turned 5, she insisted that I learn to play the violin, which I had no interest in doing, and she would sit with me while I practiced, humiliating me every time I made a mistake until I cried. She would only speak to me this way when my dad was at work, and she always told me that I could never tell him about what she said to me, or else I'd get in trouble.

I was a pretty extroverted, rambunctious toddler, but I was always kind to everyone I met, and I was as responsible as one could be at that age. Sure, I might've been a little loud and annoying at times, but what do you expect from a toddler? It never made sense why she would insult me every day because everyone else in my life was telling me the exact opposite of what she said. My teachers called me their "star student," I was in the gifted program, my classmates and neighbors loved me, and many of my relatives told my parents that I was their favorite child in our family.

Eventually, I internalized my mom's comments. Since she spent more time with me than anyone else did, I figured she knew me best and I should trust her opinion of me more than theirs. I stopped caring about making friends. If what my mom said was true, they were going to leave me one day, so what was the point of putting in all the effort? Some days during recess, I would isolate myself and read, draw, or practice violin instead of hanging out with my classmates.

When middle school came around, I finally had a good group of friends, but things got worse for me mentally. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety. I don't want to get into the details, but it was the lowest point of my life. My therapist told me that it might be worth having a chat with my parents about the harm my mom's comments caused me, so I brought it up to them. My mom told me that I was just making things up, and my dad said I needed to give her some grace because she struggles to control her anger and says things she doesn't mean.

In college, things improved considerably. I went to school in my state, but I only came home briefly once every 1 to 3 weeks. My relationship with my mom was much better because of it. She rarely insulted me. I felt like a whole new person. Everything that my mom once said wouldn't happen to me did. I got a job and some research internships, I had plenty of friends, people referred to me as popular, I held multiple leadership positions in clubs, and I graduated with a 3.97 GPA in May. I should be proud of myself, right? Everything was going right for me (minus my chronic illness, which made the last two years of college pretty miserable) and yet I still felt so insecure. I never believed it when my friends told me I was smart or good-looking. I felt like I didn't deserve the grades I got. Every time something good happened to me, I heard my mom's voice in my head telling me that I didn't deserve it, and that if someone said something nice to me, they didn't mean it. I was the biggest doormat ever and would try to be so kind to everyone to the point where it was annoying because I wanted to avoid conflict. I wanted everyone to like me. Looking back, I think it made me pretty unlikeable.

Now, I feel like I have no self-esteem or sense of self, and it's so embarrassing. I used to feel so much older than other people my age, but now I feel so much younger. I feel like I'll never be able to date because no one is attracted to someone who doesn't love themself. Earlier this year, I dated a guy friend. I was pretty awkward and didn't act like myself over the course of the relationship, and I realized that it was because I was a lesbian and only liked him as a friend, but some of the awkwardness came from me not believing that I was capable of being loved. I didn't know how to show affection for other people because I didn't experience it as a child like other people did. If my mom didn't truly love me, then why would anyone else? My self-esteem is going to be a huge issue as I prepare to apply to medical school in the next year or two. I can't talk confidently about myself in interviews. When I was training for my new job a few weeks ago, my manager mentioned that I looked nervous and I should appear a bit more confident. It feels like my insecurity is more noticeable now than ever and it's making me feel even more insecure.

I don't know how to get over these feelings. I've tried therapy and it didn't help. I know my friends would understand if I vented to them, but I like keeping certain things private and I don't want to burden them. I've tried listing things I like about myself -- I'm determined, hardworking, empathetic, and passionate about helping others -- but that didn't change anything. I know I should move out and go no-contact with my parents, but it's not that simple. If I did, none of my relatives would speak to me again. I'm working part-time while I finish my pre-med classes and study for the MCAT, so I can't even afford my own place. My parents are supporting me financially through my gap years and even offered to pay for a small portion of medical school tuition. On top of that, I have chronic health issues, which I can manage by myself, but they help me out every once in a while when I need support. I think the emotional damage has already been done and cutting them off isn't going to fix everything.

I think my insecurity not only comes from my mom's comments when I was younger but my lack of independence. My parents always discouraged me from applying to jobs until I graduated from college. I didn't start learning to drive until I was 17, and I didn't get my license until I was 19 because my parents were always too busy to practice with me. They barely taught me how to drive on highways, and I just started driving alone last month. I'm not allowed to save up to buy my own car, I don't have access to my bank account, and every dollar I make at my job has to go towards my retirement savings. It feels like they're not letting me be an adult and I'm falling behind while others my age are growing up. I avoid talking about these topics around other people because I don't want to seem immature and lazy, even though none of this is my fault and I'm actively trying to work and drive.

I don't know where to go from here. I feel so childish for continuing to let my mom's behavior affect me. On top of all of this, I recently came to the realization that I may be trans and I just know that it's going to wreck my relationship with my mom if I tell her.

When I turned 5, she insisted that I learn to play the violin, which I had no interest in doing, and she would sit with me while I practiced, humiliating me every time I made a mistake until I cried. She would only speak to me this way when my dad was at work, and she always told me that I could never tell him about what she said to me, or else I'd get in trouble.

I was a pretty extroverted, rambunctious toddler, but I was always kind to everyone I met, and I was as responsible as one could be at that age. Sure, I might've been a little loud and annoying at times, but what do you expect from a toddler? It never made sense why she would insult me every day because everyone else in my life was telling me the exact opposite of what she said. My teachers called me their "star student," I was in the gifted program, my classmates and neighbors loved me, and many of my relatives told my parents that I was their favorite child in our family.

Eventually, I internalized my mom's comments. Since she spent more time with me than anyone else did, I figured she knew me best and I should trust her opinion of me more than theirs. I stopped caring about making friends. If what my mom said was true, they were going to leave me one day, so what was the point of putting in all the effort? Some days during recess, I would isolate myself and read, draw, or practice violin instead of hanging out with my classmates.

When middle school came around, I finally had a good group of friends, but things got worse for me mentally. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety. I don't want to get into the details, but it was the lowest point of my life. My therapist told me that it might be worth having a chat with my parents about the harm my mom's comments caused me, so I brought it up to them. My mom told me that I was just making things up, and my dad said I needed to give her some grace because she struggles to control her anger and says things she doesn't mean.

In college, things improved considerably. I went to school in my state, but I only came home briefly once every 1 to 3 weeks. My relationship with my mom was much better because of it. She rarely insulted me. I felt like a whole new person. Everything that my mom once said wouldn't happen to me did. I got a job and some research internships, I had plenty of friends, people referred to me as popular, I held multiple leadership positions in clubs, and I graduated with a 3.97 GPA in May. I should be proud of myself, right? Everything was going right for me (minus my chronic illness, which made the last two years of college pretty miserable) and yet I still felt so insecure. I never believed it when my friends told me I was smart or good-looking. I felt like I didn't deserve the grades I got. Every time something good happened to me, I heard my mom's voice in my head telling me that I didn't deserve it, and that if someone said something nice to me, they didn't mean it. I was the biggest doormat ever and would try to be so kind to everyone to the point where it was annoying because I wanted to avoid conflict. I wanted everyone to like me. Looking back, I think it made me pretty unlikeable.

Now, I feel like I have no self-esteem or sense of self, and it's so embarrassing. I used to feel so much older than other people my age, but now I feel so much younger. I feel like I'll never be able to date because no one is attracted to someone who doesn't love themself. Earlier this year, I dated a guy friend. I was pretty awkward and didn't act like myself over the course of the relationship, and I realized that it was because I was a lesbian and only liked him as a friend, but some of the awkwardness came from me not believing that I was capable of being loved. I didn't know how to show affection for other people because I didn't experience it as a child like other people did. If my mom didn't truly love me, then why would anyone else? I was so happy. I wouldn’t change my childhood for anything. But as I got older the feelings of dread, anxiety, fear, depression, and suicide have taken over. 

It all started when I was in seventh grade. It was the day before my father's birthday, a Sunday. My mother, brother, and myself all went out, we picked out the perfect funfetti cake mix, pork chops and mash potatoes for dinner, and navy and white new balances all his favorite things for a day to celebrate him. He was at home while we were out. Probably in his big brown recliner, watching tv or playing on his phone. He was a simple man, a gentle giant is how people described him. We were out all day long while he was at the house. When we got home, my mom started cooking dinner and baking the cake, while I helped my brother wrap the shoes. We were so excited to celebrate with him. I know you aren’t supposed to have favorites but he was mine. We ate, sang, and opened gifts. He loved those shoes. He had an older pair he had worn to the ground, and he was so excited to wear them the next day. We were a happy family. 

We moved to our living room and watched a little tv, my brother breaking off to play Mario in the room over. I had my ACT Aspires the next day at school, so my mom turned on Hawaii 5’o. She told me it was time to go to bed and I couldn’t watch the show anyways because it would give me nightmares. I, being an angsty pre teen, persisted, I just wanted to spend time with them. But she told me it was time to go to bed so I could do well on my test. I over reacted and didn’t think anything of it, my dad chimed in and told me to listen to my mom, and I looked at him and said “I hate you”. I didn’t think twice and knew he wouldn’t take it to heart and it would be fine tomorrow. I went to the other room with my brother and laid down on the floor to protest going to bed. I nodded off to sleep….. “SARAH”. 

I was jolted awake to my mother yelling my name. I was angry that I was woken up and called in there after I was told to leave…. “SARAH”. I get up and trudge in there half asleep the teenage mutant ninja turtle blanket over my head like a hood. I am ready to throw an attitude as soon as I get in there. But I see my mother's face covered in tears, and my father on the floor. Something he often did with him being six eleven he liked to stretch out. But I knew something was wrong but I wasn’t sure what it was. She yelled again for me to get my aunt from next door. I ran, I ran like I have never ran before. Our houses only being maybe 30 feet apart, but it felt like a mile. I couldn’t see I was crying and not sure what I was crying for yet. I reached her door. I banged and banged, and she answered in her robe. She instantly knew something was wrong, and we ran back to our house. 

My mother is crying over my father. My aunt called 9-11. I sat there looking at my dad, the tears blurring everything. I saw his body so still, almost peaceful. Everything around me slowed down, the ambulance's sirens rang through our little neighborhood. Our neighbors all came out to their porches to see what was happening. I sat in our doorway holding the door open. I watched the cops, paramedics, and stretcher come in. People stopped and talked to me, I couldn’t hear them. I then watched as the cops, paramedics and stretcher left, this time with my dad on it. My neighbors came over from across the street and put me and my brother to bed. I couldn’t sleep. My mind was racing. It was racing with the most naive things. I was worried about my ACT Aspire, What was happening. What I was gonna do. He’s dead. He’s alive. To the point of exhaustion. I am again woken up by my mother. I see her and my dad's sister, they are both giving me a small smile. I have so much hope. They are going to tell me everything's all right. But then she says it, the words I never wanted to hear. “Your daddy is with grandma”. I don’t cry, I don’t move, I am quiet and motionless. I don’t know what to do. 

I sit in my room for the next 4 staring at the wall. I don’t move, shower, or eat. I rot away. People come and go but I don’t say a thing, I still don’t know what is happening. His visitation is on day 5. This is the first time I have left my room in days. My aunt gets me ready and dresses me. I sit in the front row, and I watch as people come through all giving me my condolences. I don’t say a word. I don’t force a smile. I stay looking at the casket in front of me. After everyone is gone but family, I go to his casket. I see him. This is the last time I will ever see my Dad. I hug him so tight, but it's cold. I don’t want to let go. I stay there for hours, it seems until my mom has to pry me off. Day 6 his funeral. Our catholic church is packed. I have never seen so many people there before, leaving only standing room. Everyone knew my dad, and it showed. I was wearing my little black dress and flats. I still hadn’t spoken or cried. I was so numb to what was happening. People spoke, people laughed at old stories and people cried. I sat in the front row again, not a word or tear leaving me. We drive to the burial and we go by his work and everyone that was at work is standing on the side of the road bowing their head as the funeral procession goes by. Some may have only seen him passing but still showed their respect. We buried him, and a day later I was back at school. The day after that I am taking my ACT Aspire in a room with just my teacher. 

Time didn’t stop for me. Why should I stop for any one else, why would I let others hold me back.
