TL;DR: My wife and I have been together for 6 years and married for 3. Over the course of our relationship there have been repeated issues with dishonesty, omissions, and what feels like trickle-truthing, including a 5-month relationship she had during our relationship. We are both in individual therapy and couples counseling, but I still feel like I do not have enough information to understand what happened or rebuild trust. I am emotionally exhausted, increasingly resentful, and beginning to consider divorce while still wanting to save the marriage. I am looking for advice from people who have experienced reconciliation after major trust issues.

I (45M) have been with my wife (35F) for 6 years and married for 3. We are both in individual therapy and currently participating in couples counseling.

Throughout our relationship there have been multiple incidents involving dishonesty, omissions, and what I would describe as trickle-truthing. These have included continued communication with an ex early in our relationship, hidden social media connections with former intimate acquaintances, and situations where information only came out after repeated questioning.

The largest issue for me is that my wife has admitted to having a 5-month relationship with another person during our relationship. She has admitted this directly to me and in therapy, but she has provided very few details about what that relationship actually consisted of.

I have asked for a timeline and written account. I am not asking for every text message or every detail. I am trying to understand:

When it started and ended  
The nature of the relationship  
What was hidden from me  
Why it was hidden  
What role it played in her life

My wife says she does not remember many details and that shame makes discussing it difficult.

She describes her previous relationship as toxic and says she developed habits of lying, hiding things, and self-preservation during that period. I understand that people bring unhealthy coping mechanisms into new relationships, but it has now been years, and I struggle with feeling like these issues have still not been fully addressed.

Part of what makes this difficult is that this relationship occurred while we were building what eventually became our marriage. I feel like I am being asked to forgive something that I still do not fully understand.

Over the years I have tried to be very specific about what I need:

Honest answers  
Transparency  
Accountability  
Emotional support  
A timeline and explanation of what happened  
The ability to discuss my hurt without defensiveness  
Respect for boundaries that we agreed upon  
Initiative in repairing the relationship instead of waiting for me to repeatedly raise concerns

I have also worked on myself. Historically I became the caretaker and peacekeeper in the relationship. I would carry the emotional burden, repeatedly explain my feelings, and try to keep the relationship functioning.

I have intentionally stepped away from that role. I now communicate my needs clearly and then observe whether those needs are being addressed.

The problem is that I do not feel they are.

When I bring up my feelings, I often experience defensiveness, explanations, or withdrawal. My goal is usually to understand and heal, not punish or repeatedly relive the past. Instead, I often leave those conversations feeling unheard, unsafe, insecure, and unable to trust.

One theme that I continue to come back to is self-preservation. From my perspective, many of the difficult moments in our relationship seem to involve protecting oneself rather than protecting the relationship.

When problems arise, I often experience defensiveness, minimizing, withholding information, avoidance, or shutting down. As a result, I frequently feel that preserving emotional safety for the relationship becomes secondary to avoiding discomfort, shame, conflict, or consequences.

My wife has acknowledged that self-protection has been a significant issue for her, and I understand where some of those behaviors may have originated. However, I continue to struggle with whether self-preservation is still taking priority over transparency, accountability, and rebuilding trust.

This may be the issue I struggle with most. I can understand mistakes, poor decisions, and unhealthy coping mechanisms. What I struggle to understand is feeling that protecting oneself continues to take precedence over protecting the relationship.

At this point I feel emotionally exhausted. I feel increasingly resentful because I still feel responsible for pursuing understanding and driving these conversations years later.

Part of me believes there is still information being withheld. Given the history of omissions and trickle-truthing, I struggle to trust that “I don’t remember” truly means there is nothing more to disclose.

At the same time, I recognize that I may be holding onto something that is preventing me from moving forward.

I have even considered a polygraph, not because I think it would fix the marriage, but because I feel stuck between believing there is more information and not knowing how to determine whether that is true.

I believe I have an anxious attachment style and my wife tends to be more avoidant. The more uncertain I feel, the more I pursue answers. The more I pursue, the more she seems to withdraw.

Although we are living together, I do not feel that the underlying issues have been resolved. To me, sharing a home is not the same thing as rebuilding trust.

I am also at the point where I have begun considering divorce. Not as an ultimatum, but because my resentment continues to grow and I no longer feel emotionally safe, secure, or able to trust.

I still want to work on the marriage. I am still attending counseling. However, I also need to be honest with myself that I am no longer simply frustrated. I am beginning to question whether I can remain in a marriage where I do not feel safe, secure, or able to trust.

Part of what I am trying to understand is whether I am holding onto something that can still be repaired or whether I am delaying an outcome that may ultimately be necessary.

What I am looking for advice on:

How do you rebuild trust when you feel important information is still missing?  
At what point do you accept that your partner may genuinely not remember details?  
How do you distinguish between self-protection and genuine memory issues?  
What actions would you need to see to believe reconciliation is actually progressing?  
For those who have reconciled after significant dishonesty, what actually helped you move forward?  
How do you know whether you are appropriately seeking understanding or whether resentment has simply reached a point where the relationship cannot recover?

I am genuinely looking for advice from people who have experienced something similar, especially those who have successfully reconciled after major trust issues.

2020 Christmas time.

I was at work, wrapping putting stickers on packages as I get the text from my older brother.

“Hey have you heard from dad recently?”

I stop and I think. I close out of his message and go to my dad and I’s chat.

“No, not for a few days.”

“Ok.. he hasn’t answered me I think I will go over and check on him”

I keep working. Anxiety fills because if my brother is going over there he’s worried. My brother doesn’t worry like I do.

“Okay let me know if he’s ok”

A little while goes by, still working. Checking my phone here and there.

“There was an ambulance pulling in right as I was. They took him”

I felt hot and maybe even a little sweaty. What happened? Where’s my little brother? Where is my step mom? I knew it had to do with his drinking.

“What’s going on? Where’s ___ and _____?”

This conversation was so vivid.

I left work. I don’t have clear memory of what happened in between. I remember being in the waiting room of the hospital with my little brother. I remember grabbing his phone to check something, and seeing he texted my step mom-

“Dads moaning and swearing a lot”

“He can’t talk why do I do”

“He is in his room”

She wasn’t there. My dad and younger brother there alone. For a while it was up on the air if he had called EMS. 8 years old.

That’s what I remember. That was the beginning.

I don’t know how to give much background without writing a novel but I’m trying. (Time frames are going by my age because that’s how I best describe it)

Parents divorced when I was 7. Both remarried quickly. My dad and step mom had a kid together several years later. My step mother was an alcoholic that eventually rubbed off onto my dad and he became that himself. I remember being a little kid and thinking this woman was an evil step mother that made everyone love her, but behind closed doors she was Satan herself. Hindsight is so funny.

Through the years it just got worse. There was never an evening where he was sober. I remember the dread, panic, and disappointment when I heard his words slur. Just for one night he couldn’t be sober?

My step mom would be drunk and dress me up, in her clothes, teaching me “how to walk and act the right way.” So odd. I’m like 10 at this point so I go along with it.

My dad and her would drunk argue and she was mean. I saw her once punch my dad in the stomach. I could hear them coming in and out from the garage all night. Coming back in from smoking and drinking and fighting.

I went to my mom for support. She advocated and told my dad how much this was hurting my brother and I. She validated and was and still is my best friend.

I blocked out so much time that I don’t remember a lot.

It started getting so bad that in High school I would come home to him also being home, my little brother running around in diapers doing what kids do, and he is trashed on the couch.

Id need a ride home from a friend’s and he drove drunk, so I stopped calling him.

I started making bad decisions because I knew he was too drunk to realize/care.

What made me most upset was that he didn’t take care of the child he just had. I was scared shitless for my little brother. I would voice this to my dad only to have him say lovely things-

“I can take care of my fucking kids”

“I’m not that much of a deadbeat drunk”

Followed by my personal favorites

“You just think I’m the worst father ever”

“Everything is always my fault I know I suck”

I’ll give it to him he had a 30 day run once. So he said.

I moved out around 18 and in with my mom when I couldn’t take it anymore. I had lived with her before, but moved in with my dad so I could be with my younger brother more.

I forgot about that until writing this.

I don’t remember talking to my dad much of senior year. He would text me when he was drunk asking me to bring him Taco Bell, or telling me he was such a shitty father and how much he hates his wife.

This added so much guilt.

This went on for a while. Same cycle.

Now back to 2020 Christmas time. 4 days before Christmas I was told he had like a month to live. I was devastated. I was livid. I was so scared. He spent Christmas in the hospital. I stayed with my little brother and opened presents Christmas morning while we FaceTimed him.

The new year comes, and my dad is home now.

Looking back now I was being fed false hope, by my step mom telling me that as long as he stops drinking and changes his diet he has a change to be okay. At the time I was clinging to anything I could.

This would be the last real conversation I had with my dad. He sat in his rocking chair and I sat in the couch. He didn’t even look at me, kept his eyes forward on the TV. I told him how scared I was. I told him this is it. You need help. I had found myself almost yelling at him. He just stared blankly. He said he wanted to do it himself, and he didn’t need help. I thought I had given up but I realize now he had.

This was the first and last time I had yelled at my dad.

Some time goes by, it’s really foggy but I don’t think it was 2 weeks later. He’s back in the hospital. He’s not improving and the local hospital can’t help as they need, so he gets moved out of state.

My step mom was the only one authorized for information. I think I would trust a random stranger more than her. My older brother and I tried to get as much from her as we could. We knew some but were left in the dark for the majority. The point is there was so much back and forth. I never knew if he was doing good or not.

We eventually found out he needed a new liver, shocker.

I don’t want to put too much detail but he didn’t get it, couldn’t eat for 5 months leading up to his death, signed a DNR, my step mother never went and saw him in the 6 months he was there, and told my older brother he was unloveable when he went to see him.

He died there. My step mother lied to us and said she can’t find his ashes, and then she told us his body was donated to science. The hospital reached out to her for months.

The only reason we (older brother and I) were able to get them was our last names match and no one claimed him.

We would have if we had known.

She remarried less than a year later, and moved that guy into the house my dad built.

I haven’t talked to my little brother in years.

Now I feel like I have a problem anticipating death. That’s no way to live. I’m scared of my mom dying. My wife. My brother. Of me.
